root_causes.description: The original image-ocr SKILL.md only documents generic image_to_string / image_to_data flows. It defines no keyword-priority logic, no exclusion keywords, no two-line fallback, and no numeric/date normalization for receipts. The task hint lists a very specific priority ladder (GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM/TOTAL: RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > TOTAL/AMOUNT/...) and an explicit exclusion list, none of which are codified anywhere in the skill set. The agent must reinvent all of this per run, which leads to inconsistent handling of 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' vs final rounded 'TOTAL:' lines (077) and to mistaking 'Total incl. of GBT 702.00' for the authoritative total (074).

image-ocr documents a multi_pass_ocr pattern only at the full-text-concatenation level ('join all variants'), not at the field level. There is no guidance to run several PSMs/preprocessing variants and take a majority / plausibility-filtered vote on the extracted amount or date. For a receipt like 074 where one pass yields 702.00 and multiple other sources on the same receipt (Subtotal, Payment, Total Rounded) read 102.00, a per-field voting / sanity-check step would correct the misread.

No skill specifies how to disambiguate DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY for receipts (which are Malaysian in this corpus and use DD/MM). There is also no rule to prefer the date nearest the 'Date:' / 'Invoice' label, no OCR-digit sanity filter (e.g. month > 12 implies the other interpretation), and no rule to reject obviously corrupted dates in favor of a secondary candidate elsewhere on the receipt. This causes 034's date to come out transposed.

The original xlsx SKILL.md focuses on financial-model color coding, formula hygiene, and recalc; it does not describe the 'strict-schema, graded-line-by-line' output contract this task uses. In particular it does not say: write Python None (never ''/'nan'/'None') on extraction failure, write amounts as strings with exactly two decimals, use a specific sheet name, use index=False, and verify by re-reading. The 078 cell holding '' (empty string) rather than a real null is a direct consequence.

Even with keyword priority, the skills do not teach the semantic rule 'prefer the final rounded / post-adjustment TOTAL over an earlier Inclusive-GST line when both are present on the same receipt'. This is what breaks 077 (23.26 vs 23.25 after rounding -0.01). Related: there is no exclusion for lines like 'Total Item(s):', 'Total Savings', 'Total Gross', or 'Total Sales Incl GST' when a later strict 'TOTAL' line exists, so agent heuristics keep diverging across runs.

openai-vision is loaded but the skills do not describe when/how to invoke vision as a fallback when Tesseract confidence is low or when per-field voting disagrees. For borderline receipts (074, 078) a documented escalation path 'if Tesseract per-field confidence < threshold OR amount regex yields multiple incompatible candidates, call openai-vision with a strict JSON schema for date+total' would recover accuracy without changing the primary pipeline.

defects: No codified receipt field-extraction logic (priority tiers, exclusions, two-line fallback).
Multi-pass OCR described only as text-concatenation, not as per-field voting/consensus.
No date normalization helper (format detection, DD/MM vs MM/DD disambiguation, ISO output).
No null-safe per-image pipeline that returns None on failure instead of empty strings.
No deterministic filename-ordered batch iterator restricted to image extensions.

No 'strict-schema output' section covering: exact sheet name, exact column order, index=False, lexicographic row order, string-typed numeric fields, real None (not '', 'nan', 'None'), and a round-trip verification step.
Guidance privileges formulas-over-values, which is actively wrong for graders that compare literal cell contents.
No warning about pandas default NaN leaking into cells as the string 'nan' under some readers.
No documented escalation protocol from Tesseract to vision for low-confidence receipt fields.
No strict-JSON prompt template for extracting {date_iso, total_amount_two_decimals} with explicit null semantics.
Out of scope for this task; no changes required beyond leaving it unchanged.

changes: Add a 'Structured Field Extraction (Receipts/Forms)' section that defines ordered priority tiers (GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL:RM/TOTAL RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > NETT/NET TOTAL / TOTAL DUE / AMOUNT DUE / BALANCE DUE / bare TOTAL / bare AMOUNT) and an EXCLUSIONS list (SUBTOTAL, SUB TOTAL, TAX, GST, SST, DISCOUNT, CHANGE, CASH TENDERED) that is evaluated BEFORE tier matching.
Specify a two-line fallback: if the matched keyword line has no numeric value, scan the next non-empty, non-excluded line and take its last number.
Mandate output types: amount as str formatted via f"{v:.2f}" with commas and currency symbols stripped; date as ISO YYYY-MM-DD; None on any failure, never '' or 'nan'.

root_causes.description: Priority tiers collapse 'Total (Inclusive of GST)', 'Net Total', 'Total Amt Rounded', and a final bold 'TOTAL:' into one generic \\bTOTAL\\b tier. On receipts with a Rounding Adj line, the oracle tracks the post-rounding standalone TOTAL, which must outrank any earlier 'Total (incl. of GST)' line.

When several lines mention TOTAL, the extractor picks the last keyword hit regardless of whether its number is corroborated anywhere else in the receipt. OCR corruption on one isolated line (e.g. '——S«702.00') therefore wins over three agreeing 102.00 lines.

Extraction correctly returns None on failure, but the Excel writer path did not coerce None to an empty/real-null cell; a '' sneaks through. The xlsx skill's strict-schema checklist says 'write None not ""' but has no copy-paste writer that guarantees it, and no self-check that re-reads the file and asserts non-null cells are real strings.

Date extraction stops on the first regex hit from the first OCR variant. For receipts with glyph ambiguity (3/8, 0/O, 1/l), different PSMs produce different digits; without cross-variant voting or anchor-word scoping ('Date :'), the first noisy answer wins.

Skills live only as preloaded markdown; the agent is not routed through them for receipt tasks. With 65 iterations consumed on ad-hoc regex tuning in extract.py, the batch terminated at max_iterations instead of a natural stop, meaning any late-stage refinement (null-writing, voting) never executed.

defects: TOTAL_PRIORITY lacks a dedicated tier for a final standalone 'TOTAL:' line that appears below a 'Rounding Adj' / 'Total Rounded' / 'Total After Adj' row; 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' is treated as equally specific.

No rule to deprioritize candidate lines whose OCR text around the number contains obvious noise (long runs of dashes/underscores, non-ASCII punctuation fused to digits) — exactly the '——S«702.00' pattern.
No cross-line corroboration: when the same amount appears on Subtotal/Payment/Total-incl-GST, that amount should be preferred over an isolated keyword hit.
Multi-pass OCR described but not required; the pipeline is still single-pass. No voting/agreement logic across PSM variants for either date or total.

Date extraction returns the first regex match in reading order with no preference for a line that actually starts with a 'Date' / 'Tarikh' / 'Invoice Date' anchor, so random ID numbers or OCR-garbled dates can win.
Strict-schema section warns against '' / 'None' / 'NaN' but does not supply a mandatory 'write and verify' helper that converts any falsy-but-not-None value (including '') to None before to_excel.
The post-write verification snippet checks shape and dtype but does not assert that total_amount cells are either None or a str matching ^\d+\.\d{2}$; a stray '' would pass the current checks.

No explicit statement that pandas NaN must be replaced with None via df.where(pd.notna(df), None) or astype(object).where(...) before writing to openpyxl, which is the common path through which '' and NaN leak in.

Not referenced from image-ocr as a disagreement-breaker for low-confidence Tesseract outputs (e.g. date digit confusion, or when two PSM variants disagree on the total). A brief cross-reference would let the ocr pipeline escalate ambiguous fields rather than guessing.

skill_defects.defect: Missing a structured, generalizable receipt-field extraction recipe: priority-keyword tiers (GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM/TOTAL:RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > TOTAL/AMOUNT/NET TOTAL/BALANCE DUE/…), exclusion-keyword prefilter (SUBTOTAL, SUB TOTAL, TAX, GST, SST, DISCOUNT, CHANGE, CASH TENDERED, and the GST-exclusion variants like 'Total (Excluding …)'), numeric pattern that recognises 1,234.56 / 1234.56 and prefers tokens with exactly two decimal digits, two-line fallback for 'keyword on one line / amount on the next', and normalization to a string with exactly two decimals with None on failure.

No tie-break policy when multiple candidates match within one priority tier. Should document: within a tier, prefer the LAST matching line in reading order as the baseline (keyword hierarchy already discriminates subtotal from grand total), but (a) cross-check across multiple OCR passes and prefer values that agree across passes, and (b) if a value is inconsistent with an unambiguous nearby anchor (Subtotal/Payment/Cash both equal X while the candidate differs by a single-digit substitution), prefer the anchor-consistent value. Also document the specific pitfall that 'Total Amt Rounded' / 'Rounded Total' lines are valid grand-total candidates but are OCR-brittle.

No explicit date extraction recipe. Should specify: scan in reading order; prefer lines explicitly labelled 'Date' (strip the label before parsing); try a fixed list of patterns (DD/MM/YYYY, DD-MM-YYYY, DD/MM/YY, DD-MM-YY, YYYY-MM-DD, DD Mon YYYY, DD-Mon-YYYY); reject matches whose month>12 or day>31; return None on failure; never guess locale-ambiguous dates; normalise to ISO YYYY-MM-DD.

Multi-pass OCR section mentions variants but does not call out 2x upscaling as a standard variant and does not say how to combine outputs. For small/low-DPI receipts, upscaling (bicubic/LANCZOS 2x) plus PSM 6 is the single most impactful variant. Skill should list it first and describe simple consensus: run default and upscaled+autocontrast+PSM6, extract fields from both, and prefer the value that appears in both passes.

The candidate (explicit_method_draft) version added structured sections but still (a) picks the first regex match for dates with no label preference or plausibility check, (b) uses the first line matching a tier with last-number-on-that-line instead of also searching later lines in the same tier or returning a candidate list, and (c) does not describe multi-pass consensus or the 'exactly 2 decimals' preference that the source agent proved necessary. These should be added so the recipe generalizes.

Original skill lacks a 'strict-schema extraction output' section. Needs: exact sheet name, exact column order, index=False, real None (not "" / "nan"), string dtype preservation for numeric-looking fields that must keep trailing zeros, lexicographic sort by filename, verification by re-reading the written workbook. The candidate xlsx revision already contains most of this and should be retained.

No guidance that pandas' NaN handling will coerce missing string cells in unpredictable ways; must explicitly assign Python None to the DataFrame cells and use .astype('object') for the numeric-string column so .to_excel writes an empty cell rather than 'nan' / "".

repair_recommendations.change: Add a top-level 'Receipt field extraction pipeline' section documenting: (1) ordered priority tiers exactly matching the task family — [GRAND TOTAL], [TOTAL RM, TOTAL: RM], [TOTAL AMOUNT], [NETT TOTAL, NET TOTAL, TOTAL DUE, AMOUNT DUE, BALANCE DUE, TOTAL, AMOUNT]; (2) exclusion list — SUBTOTAL, SUB TOTAL, TAX, GST, SST, DISCOUNT, CHANGE, CASH TENDERED, plus 'EXCLUDING' / 'EXCL.' / 'EXCL GST' as GST-exclusion subtotal markers; (3) exclusion check BEFORE keyword match; (4) numeric pattern that matches '1,234.56' and '1234.56' and prefers tokens with exactly two decimal digits; (5) two-line fallback: if the keyword line has no numeric match, use the last number on the next non-empty, non-excluded line; (6) return a string formatted with exactly two decimals (f'{v:.2f}') after stripping commas and currency; (7) return None on any failure. Keep code generic (regex tiers in a list of lists) so it generalizes to other receipt corpora.

Add a 'Multi-pass OCR and candidate consensus' subsection. Mandate running at least two passes: (a) default Tesseract on the raw image; (b) 2x LANCZOS upscale + grayscale + autocontrast + '--psm 6'. From each pass extract (tier_index, value) for the total and a candidate list for the date. Prefer the value that appears in BOTH passes; if they disagree, prefer the candidate from the lower tier index; within the same tier prefer the one with exactly two decimal digits in the source string; otherwise prefer the upscaled pass (empirically higher precision on faint receipts). Do not special-case receipts — describe this as the default consensus rule.

Add a 'Date extraction' subsection: iterate lines in reading order; for each line, strip a leading 'Date' / 'Tarikh' / 'Dated' label; try an ordered list of regex+strftime patterns (DD/MM/YYYY, DD-MM-YYYY, DD/MM/YY, DD-MM-YY, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD, DD Mon YYYY, DD-Mon-YYYY); reject any parsed date whose month is not 1–12 or day is not 1–31; prefer the FIRST valid match on a line whose label is literally 'Date' (or starts with 'Date'); fall back to the first valid match anywhere; return ISO YYYY-MM-DD; return None if nothing parses. Explicitly warn against trusting lines beginning with 'Print Date', 'Closed', 'FRN ON', 'Salesperson', or those appearing after a payment/change line.

Document the 'rounded total vs inclusive total' tie-break: when both 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' and a plain 'TOTAL:' / 'Total After Rounding' / 'Rounded Total' appear in the same priority tier, prefer the rounded/final one (last matching line) because that is what cashiers charge. Pair this with the consensus rule so OCR-corrupted rounded lines (e.g., '702.00' vs repeated '102.00') are overridden when the non-rounded candidate is corroborated by an unambiguous anchor (Subtotal / Payment / Cash / Change-implied total).

Add a short 'When to escalate to vision OCR' note cross-referencing openai-vision: if Tesseract returns None for the total or if date month>12/day>31 after consensus, optionally run a single-field targeted vision call on the receipt image asking only for that one field in ISO format or 'N.NN'. Keep this optional; do not require network access.

Keep and tighten the 'Strict-Schema Outputs' section in the candidate draft. Explicitly require: exactly one sheet with the task-specified name; columns in task-specified order with index=False; missing values as Python None (never '', 'None', 'nan', NaN); numeric-string fields written via .astype('object') so trailing zeros are preserved; rows sorted lexicographically by filename; and a self-verify step that re-reads the workbook, asserts sheet name, column order, row order, and spot-checks one non-null formatted value. Add a pitfall bullet: 'pandas will coerce NaN to "nan" when the column dtype is inferred as string; assign None after building the DataFrame and set dtype=object for the affected columns.'

Add a cross-reference from xlsx to image-ocr for receipt/extraction tasks, and from image-ocr to xlsx for strict-schema output. This reduces cross-skill search iterations and prevents the agent from writing '' where the grader expects an empty cell.

Add a brief 'Single-field fallback for OCR pipelines' subsection: given an image and a field spec ('date as YYYY-MM-DD or null', 'total as N.NN or null'), return exactly that one value as JSON. Document token/cost caveats. Referenced by image-ocr as an escalation path only — do not change the default pipeline.

Priority-tier voting selects the final 'Rounded Total' line via last-candidate preference and returns 702.00 instead of 102.00. Image confirms final rounded total is 102.00.

Image shows receipt with 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26', 'Rounding Adj: -0.01', 'TOTAL: 23.25'. The prediction returned 23.26 (the pre-rounding total). The task says to prefer the final/rounded total; the last 'TOTAL:' line (23.25) should win over the earlier 'Total (Inclusive of GST):' line.

Image clearly shows 'Total : 92.80' and 'Grand Total : 92.80'. Default OCR variant yields tier-3 value 92.80, but combined voting across upscaled variants 1/2 where 'Grand Total' line lost its number promoted a fallback tier-0 'Grand Total' → next-line 'Cash Received 100.00' to value 100.00, and prediction_present row shows an empty string instead of null. Two defects: (a) fallback to adjacent non-excluded line can pick up CASH/payment amounts because 'CASH RECEIVED' is not in the exclusion list; (b) missing values are serialized as '' not real nulls.

Image shows 'Date: 09/03/2018' (and the printed invoice marker A03/1 corroborates March). Prediction parsed it as 2018-08-09, indicating the DD/MM/YYYY date 09/03/2018 was interpreted as MM/DD or OCR read '03' as '08'. Trajectory also shows an alternate OCR variant read the date as '09/08/2018'. The current date pipeline accepts the first regex hit without disambiguation or cross-variant voting on the date.

Row for 078.jpg in the delivered predictions has total_amount='' (empty string) rather than a real null cell. Candidate xlsx skill already warns this fails line-by-line grading; the agent's write path is not coercing None to a real null.

root_causes.summary: Multi-variant OCR voting conflates OCR noise with real receipt content for totals.
root_causes.detail: The explicit_method_draft image-ocr skill describes a single-pass priority/exclusion pipeline, but the agent implemented a 3-variant (default / autocontrast / 2x upscale) voter with a 'prefer last keyword candidate, then fall back to next non-empty non-excluded line' rule. Upscaling frequently mutates digits (e.g., 86.17→688.17, 102.00→702.00, 92.80→100.00 via fallback to CASH line). Neither the current image-ocr nor xlsx SKILL gives guidance on how to combine variants, so the agent invented a brittle rule.

root_causes.summary: Exclusion list is incomplete for payment/tender lines, so fallback-to-next-line leaks CASH/VISA amounts.
root_causes.detail: image-ocr lists EXCLUSIONS = ['SUBTOTAL','SUB TOTAL','TAX','GST','SST','DISCOUNT','CHANGE','CASH TENDERED']. The fallback 'if keyword line has no number, use last number on next non-empty non-excluded line' then accepts 'Visa RM =688.17', 'Cash Received 100.00', etc., because 'CASH', 'CASH RECEIVED', 'VISA', 'MASTERCARD', 'PAYMENT', 'CARD', 'TENDERED' (alone), 'ROUNDING' are not listed. The two-line fallback described in the task is intended for keyword-and-number-split layouts, not for jumping over the number line into payment lines.

root_causes.summary: No preference for the final 'rounded/net' total when multiple same-tier totals appear.
root_causes.detail: image-ocr defines a single tier for 'TOTAL', 'AMOUNT', 'NET TOTAL', 'NETT TOTAL', 'TOTAL DUE', etc., and picks the last candidate in reading order. When a receipt prints 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' then 'Rounding Adj: -0.01' then 'TOTAL: 23.25', last-in-reading-order will usually be correct, but when the preprocessed OCR reorders or the final 'TOTAL:' line is garbled, the earlier Inclusive line wins. There is no explicit sub-ordering such as 'prefer ROUNDED/NET/FINAL TOTAL over INCLUSIVE/SUB totals when both are in the same tier, and prefer the last keyword hit in document order within a file'.

root_causes.summary: Date parsing is ambiguity-naive and does not use multi-variant agreement.
root_causes.detail: image-ocr's DATE_PATTERNS tries %d/%m/%Y first and returns the earliest regex match; it does not vote across OCR variants, does not detect when the same visual date is read differently (e.g., '09/03/2018' vs '09/08/2018'), and does not prefer a date that appears near explicit 'Date:' / 'DATE:' / 'Invoice Date' markers. Multi-variant date voting exists in the agent's draft code but not in the skill guidance, so the next run can regress.

root_causes.summary: xlsx strict-schema contract is documented but the agent's writer still emitted empty string for a null total.
root_causes.detail: The explicit_method_draft xlsx skill has a strong Strict-Schema section telling the writer to convert None/NaN to real nulls, cast total_amount to object dtype, and verify by re-reading. Despite this, the delivered row for 078.jpg has total_amount=''. The skill's canonical pattern is correct, but it does not forbid the common 'pd.DataFrame.fillna("")' or openpyxl 'cell.value = ""' anti-patterns, nor does it include a post-write assertion that every None stays as a Python None (not '' or 'nan') when re-read.

root_causes.summary: Budget/termination pressure amplified brittle heuristics.
root_causes.detail: Source run hit max_iterations (65) with termination_reason='max_iterations' after many debug cycles tweaking regex/voting. The skills do not guide the agent to (a) stop expanding OCR variants once marginal returns are negative or (b) prefer a small, well-exclusion-covered single pipeline over ensembling. This structural gap caused the agent to keep adding variants that introduced the 074/078 regressions.

skill_defects.defect: Exclusion list is too narrow: missing CASH (standalone), CASH RECEIVED, CARD, VISA, MASTERCARD, DEBIT, CREDIT, PAYMENT, TENDER, TENDERED, ROUNDING, ROUNDING ADJ, SERV(ICE) CHARGE, BALANCE, POINTS. Two-line fallback should also treat payment/tender lines as exclusions.

Priority tiers do not distinguish final-rounded totals from inclusive/subtotal-like totals. No explicit ordering such as: GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM / ROUNDED TOTAL / NET TOTAL / NETT TOTAL / TOTAL AMOUNT > TOTAL (INCLUSIVE OF GST) > TOTAL (EXCLUDING GST) > bare TOTAL/AMOUNT, and no 'prefer the last keyword hit within the same tier, excluding keyword hits that are clearly summary/section-start lines (e.g., 'GST SUMMARY')'.

No guidance for combining multiple OCR variants. The skill should either (a) prescribe a single robust pipeline (grayscale + autocontrast + --psm 6, optional 2x upscale only when first pass fails) or (b) specify a safe voting rule: vote on the extracted (tier, value) pair, require agreement from ≥2 variants before overriding the default-pass result, and never allow a lower-priority variant to upgrade the tier.

Two-line fallback is unbounded and symmetric. It should (a) restrict to the immediately next non-empty line, (b) require that line to contain a monetary token (digits with 2 decimals or comma-grouped), and (c) skip the fallback entirely if the keyword line itself contains any digits at all (partial OCR noise).

Date extraction lacks (a) anchor-keyword preference ('Date', 'Invoice Date', 'Tarikh', 'Print Date' etc.), (b) cross-variant agreement when multiple OCR passes are used, and (c) ambiguity handling for %d/%m vs %m/%d (e.g., when day>12 is unambiguous, lock the format for the rest of the file; when both are ≤12, prefer the format that is consistent with other receipts in the batch and with any nearby month name tokens).

The skill does not require returning strings already formatted to the task's contract (2-decimal string, ISO date) and does not say to strip trailing/leading whitespace, currency prefixes, or decimal commas before formatting. The current regex already handles thousands separators but the skill text does not say 'remove any non-digit, non-dot, non-comma, non-minus characters adjacent to the number before conversion'.

Strict-Schema section does not include a MANDATORY post-write re-read assertion that every intended-None cell reads back as a real null (pd.isna) and not '' / 'None' / 'nan'. It should also explicitly forbid df.fillna('') and openpyxl assignments of empty strings for missing values, and recommend pd.NA / None with object dtype.

Strict-Schema canonical pattern does not call out that total_amount must come from the extractor as a str or None (never float, never NaN) and that an upstream bug producing '' should be caught at the DataFrame boundary (e.g., df.replace({'': None}) before to_excel).

Neither skill tells the agent when to stop iterating on OCR heuristics. Given a fixed iteration budget, the skill should prescribe: 'if the first full pass produces an output that passes the Strict-Schema contract (valid shape, valid types, every non-null total matches /^\d+\.\d{2}$/, every non-null date matches /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/), stop and ship; only iterate if the self-check fails.' This would have prevented the 074/078 regressions introduced by late ensembling.

Apply the exclusion check both to the keyword line and to the next-line fallback. Document why these payment/tender lines must never become a total via fallback.
repair_recommendations.generalization_note: This helps any receipt task where OCR noise degrades the keyword line and the next line is a tender/payment amount.

repair_recommendations.change: Refine the priority tiers to: (T0) GRAND TOTAL; (T1) TOTAL RM / TOTAL: RM / RM TOTAL; (T2) ROUNDED TOTAL / TOTAL ROUNDED / TOTAL AMT ROUNDED / NET TOTAL / NETT TOTAL / TOTAL (ROUNDED); (T3) TOTAL AMOUNT / AMOUNT DUE / BALANCE DUE / TOTAL DUE; (T4) TOTAL (INCLUSIVE OF GST) / TOTAL INCL. OF GST / TOTAL INCLUDING GST / TOTAL SALES; (T5) bare TOTAL / AMOUNT. Within a tier, prefer the LAST match in document order; across tiers, lower T wins. Explicitly exclude lines that are section headers like 'GST SUMMARY', 'TAX SUMMARY', 'TOTAL ITEM(S)', 'TOTAL QTY', 'TOT QTY', 'ITEM COUNT' (treat these as exclusions).
repair_recommendations.generalization_note: Gives a stable ordering so that rounded/net totals win over inclusive subtotals even when both lines match the broad 'TOTAL' keyword.

repair_recommendations.change: Specify the OCR variant policy explicitly: (a) Always start with a single default pass on the original image (no upscale). (b) Extract (tier, value, raw_line) and accept it if tier<=T3 AND value matches /^\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*\.\d{2}$/ after stripping. (c) Only if the first pass returns None OR a T4/T5 result, run ONE additional pass with grayscale+autocontrast at --psm 6; prefer its result ONLY if it yields a strictly better (lower) tier. (d) Do NOT use a 2x upscale pass by default; upscaling is listed as optional only for images whose max dimension is <1000 px. (e) When combining variants, never allow a variant's tier to be upgraded by a later variant unless the extracted value appears in ≥2 variants.
repair_recommendations.generalization_note: Prevents the 074/078-style regressions where aggressive upscaling corrupts digits and promotes CASH/VISA lines.

repair_recommendations.change: Constrain the two-line fallback: trigger ONLY when the keyword line has zero digit characters at all (not just no 2-decimal number). The fallback line must (a) be the next non-empty line, (b) not be in the expanded EXCLUSIONS, (c) contain a token matching /^\s*(RM\s*)?\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*\.\d{2}\s*$/ anchored or as the only monetary token. Otherwise return None for that tier and continue.
repair_recommendations.generalization_note: Keeps the useful split-line case ('GRAND TOTAL\n 92.80') while blocking jumps to CASH/CHANGE.

repair_recommendations.change: Add a date-extraction policy: (a) Prefer dates that are on or immediately after a line containing an anchor keyword from {'DATE','DATE:', 'INVOICE DATE','TARIKH','PRINT DATE','TRANSACTION DATE'}; (b) Try formats in this order on the anchored substring: %d/%m/%Y, %d-%m-%Y, %d.%m.%Y, %d %b %Y, %d-%b-%Y, %Y-%m-%d, %Y/%m/%d, %d/%m/%y; (c) If day>12 in a %d/%m/... candidate, lock DMY; if month token is >12 in a %m/%d/... candidate, lock DMY; (d) When multiple OCR variants are run, vote on the ISO-normalized date and require ≥2-variant agreement to override the default pass's date; (e) Return None if no anchored date is found and the only unanchored candidate is ambiguous (both parts ≤12 and no month name).
repair_recommendations.generalization_note: Handles the 034.jpg DD/MM vs MM/DD confusion and reduces reliance on first-match-wins.

repair_recommendations.change: Mandate normalization before formatting: strip leading/trailing non-digit characters adjacent to the number, remove currency tokens ('RM', '$'), remove thousand separators (','), reject negative values for totals, reject values with more than 2 decimal digits (round only if the task explicitly says so; otherwise treat 189.673 as OCR noise and either discard or re-try with a different variant). repair_recommendations.generalization_note: Hardens contract compliance across any monetary-extraction task.

repair_recommendations.change: Strengthen the Strict-Schema section: (a) Add an explicit rule: 'missing values MUST be written as pd.NA / None; never as empty string, "None", or NaN placeholder'. (b) Add the pattern df = df.replace({'': None, 'nan': None, 'None': None}) before to_excel. (c) Add a MANDATORY verification step: after writing, re-read with pd.read_excel and assert that for every column expected to contain nullable strings, every value is either None (pd.isna True) or a non-empty str matching the required regex (e.g., /^\d+\.\d{2}$/ for 2-decimal strings, /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ for ISO dates). (d) Explicitly forbid df.fillna('') and openpyxl cell assignments to '' for missing values.
repair_recommendations.generalization_note: Prevents the 078.jpg empty-string regression on any strict-schema task.

repair_recommendations.change: Add a 'stop condition' to the Strict-Schema workflow: once the self-check passes (schema shape OK, all non-null values match required regex, filenames sorted lexicographically, row count equals input count), ship immediately and do not iterate further on extraction heuristics. If the self-check fails, iterate only on the failing rows, not on the whole pipeline.
repair_recommendations.generalization_note: Mitigates iteration-budget exhaustion observed in source run (max_iterations=65 hit).

repair_recommendations.change: Add a short 'Debug / Self-Check' section at the end that tells the agent to: (i) print the first-pass OCR for any image where extraction returned None, (ii) print the matched keyword line and the extracted token for every non-null total, (iii) sanity-check that the extracted total is <= any Cash Received / Payment / Visa amount on the same receipt (when present and parseable) — if it is greater, flag the row for re-extraction, (iv) ensure no two receipts in the batch yield identical (filename, date, total) by accident of fallback (a cheap sanity test).
repair_recommendations.generalization_note: Makes the OCR pipeline self-auditing without peeking at any oracle values.

repair_recommendations.change: In image-ocr, add a one-paragraph pointer: 'When used with the xlsx Strict-Schema output pattern, return extracted fields as (date: Optional[str in YYYY-MM-DD], total_amount: Optional[str with /^\d+\.\d{2}$/]). observed_failures.issue: Incorrect total extracted; OCR variant majority-vote picked a value that disagrees with the subtotal/payment lines visible on the receipt.
Extracted the pre-rounding 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' value instead of the final 'TOTAL' line that appears after the rounding adjustment.

Agent emitted empty string in Excel cell instead of a real null; field also failed extraction entirely because 'Grand Total' and 'Total' lines in this receipt have the amount in a separate column and OCR split them.
Date extracted does not match the receipt date; likely picked a secondary/printed date or misparsed DD/MM vs MM/DD.

root_causes.summary: OCR variant voting weights by raw count, not by cross-line corroboration
root_causes.detail: pick_best_total chose a value that appeared in more OCR variants even when the alternative value is confirmed by multiple same-receipt lines (Subtotal, Total incl., Payment). Majority vote across noisy variants beats single-variant consensus that matches the receipt structure.

root_causes.summary: Highest-priority tier wins even on a pure fallback match
root_causes.detail: When a higher-priority keyword (e.g. GRAND TOTAL) exists but its own line has no number, the split-line fallback can land on a payment/change/cash-received line. Because that tier outranks everything, a correct tier-3 TOTAL value is suppressed by a bad tier-0 fallback.

root_causes.summary: 'Last candidate wins' picks the wrong TOTAL when a 'Rounding' line follows
root_causes.detail: For receipts whose layout is Total(Inclusive) / Rounding Adj / TOTAL:, picking the LAST TOTAL-keyword line is correct, but picking the first/earlier one (pre-rounding) yields the wrong amount by a few cents. The current ordering logic plus exclusion of 'Rounding Adj' can cause the final-total line to be missed when OCR mangles it.

root_causes.summary: Missing/unparseable fields written as empty string instead of real null
root_causes.detail: The Excel writer emitted "" for 078.total_amount instead of Python None, so the cell is a non-empty string and fails exact-equality grading against an expected null.

root_causes.summary: Date extraction returns first regex match without disambiguating DD/MM vs MM/DD or multiple dates on the receipt
root_causes.detail: When a receipt contains more than one date-like token (invoice print date, transaction date, loyalty date), the earliest-match-wins strategy can select a non-primary date, and DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY ambiguity is resolved only by pattern order.

skill_defects.defect: The structured-field extraction section documents keyword priority, exclusions and a two-line fallback, but does not require (a) cross-line value corroboration when voting across OCR variants, (b) restricting the two-line fallback so it cannot land on payment/cash/visa/change lines, or (c) preferring the LAST occurrence of a TOTAL keyword when multiple appear (pre-rounding vs after-rounding).

Exclusion list does not cover common non-total lines that carry 'RM' or 'TOTAL'-adjacent wording: 'Visa', 'Mastercard', 'Cash Received', 'Cash Payment', 'Points', 'Total Gross', 'Total Sales', 'Total (Excluding ...)', 'Total Excl.'; this allows fallbacks and lower-tier matches to leak into the result.

Date extraction guidance returns the first match without a tie-break that prefers the date nearest an invoice/receipt/transaction keyword, and does not discuss DD/MM vs MM/DD disambiguation for Malaysian receipts (which are DD/MM/YYYY).
Multi-pass OCR pattern aggregates text but has no documented voting rule for combining structured fields across variants (frequency-only voting is fragile when one variant is systematically wrong).

Strict-schema section correctly says to write None for missing values and shows the canonical pattern, but does not include an explicit pre-write sanitization step that converts '', 'None', 'NaN', 'nan', or float('nan') in the rows list to Python None before to_excel, nor a post-write verification that empty-expected cells actually read back as NaN/None (not empty string).

The verification snippet checks column names, sheet name, sort order and two-decimal format, but does not assert that total_amount strings contain no currency symbols, thousand separators, or whitespace — all of which are common OCR artifacts that would silently pass the length-of-decimals check.

Not used in this run, but its 'text extraction' section does not mention it can be used as a disambiguation fallback when Tesseract confidence is low or when multiple candidate totals/dates conflict — a cheap second opinion that would have fixed 074/077/078/034.

No guidance that for strict-schema outputs the entire DataFrame should be coerced to object dtype BEFORE assigning None, otherwise pandas may upcast None to NaN in a numeric column and the grader sees a different cell value.

repair_recommendations.change: In the 'Structured Field Extraction' section, add a rule: when the keyword line has NO digits, the two-line fallback may read the next non-empty line ONLY if that line is not an exclusion line AND does not match a payment-method pattern (VISA|MASTERCARD|MASTER|AMEX|DEBIT|CREDIT|CARD|CASH|E-?WALLET|TNG|GRABPAY|POINTS|LOYALTY|RM\s*PAID|PAID|BALANCE). If the keyword line has digits but they fail to parse as a valid decimal, do NOT fall through.

Expand EXCLUSIONS to include: 'VISA', 'MASTERCARD', 'AMEX', 'DEBIT', 'CREDIT CARD', 'CASH RECEIVED', 'CASH PAYMENT', 'CASH TENDER', 'PAID', 'BALANCE', 'POINTS', 'TOTAL GROSS', 'TOTAL SALES', 'TOTAL (EXCLUDING', 'TOTAL EXCL', 'AMT EXCL', 'EXCL. observed_failures.symptom: Agent produced a date that does not correspond to the single visible 'Date: 09/03/2018' line; likely parsed a spurious date-like token (e.g., a stock code '1801' near a number) instead of the dedicated DATE line.

Image contains only 102.00 across all total-like lines (Subtotal, Total Incl. of GST, Total Amt Rounded, Payment). OCR misread '1' as '7' on the line the extractor picked; there was no cross-check against the other total lines that agreed on 102.00.

Receipt shows 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26', then 'Rounding Adj: -0.01', then a final bold 'TOTAL: 23.25'. Extractor selected the earlier 'Total ...' hit and ignored the trailing TOTAL line that follows the rounding adjustment.

Receipt has 'Total: 92.80' and 'Grand Total: 92.80'. Extractor returned nothing AND wrote an empty string into the cell instead of a real null, indicating both an extraction miss and a null-writing drift from the current xlsx guidance.

root_causes: image-ocr total-selection scans keyword tiers top-down and takes the FIRST matching line, so when a receipt has an intermediate 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' followed by a 'Rounding Adj' and a final 'TOTAL' line, the pre-rounding value wins over the true grand total.
image-ocr has no notion of 'post-rounding' total: the presence of a 'ROUNDING' / 'ROUNDING ADJ' line between two candidate totals is not used to prefer the later candidate.

image-ocr date extraction scans the whole text with generic regexes and returns the first well-formed match, with no preference for dates appearing on a line containing a DATE keyword, so stray digit groups elsewhere on the receipt can win.

image-ocr runs a single OCR/preprocessing pass per receipt; a single misread digit (1→7, O→0, etc.) silently produces a confidently-wrong amount with no cross-check against other total-bearing lines on the same receipt.

image-ocr can drop a total entirely when the OCR'd keyword line is slightly garbled and the two-line fallback only looks one line ahead; it then returns None with no second-chance scan of the bottom region of the receipt.

xlsx strict-schema pattern is in the candidate skill but the run still produced an empty string for the failed cell, indicating the guidance is not operationally sticky: missing values need to be materialised as Python None before to_excel, and verified by a re-read that the cell is truly empty.

skill_defects.defect: extract_total iterates lines top-down and short-circuits on the first match within a tier; it should prefer the LAST match within a tier (totals live at the bottom of receipts) and must prefer a TOTAL match that occurs AFTER any 'ROUNDING' / 'ROUNDING ADJ' line.

No context rule for 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' vs a later plain 'TOTAL' line; the current tiered keyword list treats them as equivalent even though the plain trailing TOTAL is the grader-aligned value.

Date extraction has no proximity-to-keyword preference (DATE, DATE:, DATED, PRINT DATE, 'Date :') and no plausibility check (year range, agreement across multiple candidate matches), so a non-date digit cluster can outrank the real date line.

Multi-pass OCR exists but is not wired into the field extractor: when extract_total fails, when it returns a value that disagrees with the other total-bearing lines on the same receipt, or when the two-line fallback is hit, the pipeline does not retry with alternate PSM / preprocessing variants.

Two-line fallback only looks at the single next line; it does not scan forward a small window (2–3 lines) for the first numeric, which is needed when OCR inserts a blank/garbage line between the keyword and the amount.

Strict-schema section describes the None vs '' rule but does not provide an enforced write-time coercion step (e.g., df.where(df.notna() & (df != ''), None) before to_excel) nor a verification assertion that failed-extraction cells are truly empty on re-read.

repair_recommendations.change: Rewrite extract_total to collect ALL matches per tier with their line indices, honour EXCLUSIONS first, then within the highest non-empty tier pick the match with the LARGEST line index (bottom-most). Fall back to the next tier only when a tier yields zero matches.

Add an explicit 'post-rounding total' rule: detect lines matching r'ROUND(ING)?(\s*ADJ(USTMENT)?)?' and, when a candidate TOTAL match exists AFTER such a rounding line, prefer it over any TOTAL match that appears before the rounding line (covers 'Total (Inclusive of GST) … Rounding Adj … TOTAL:' receipts).

Extend the two-line fallback to a small forward window (next 2–3 non-empty lines) and strip currency prefixes/noise (RM, :, |, trailing letters) before applying NUM_RE, so garbled-but-aligned amounts are still captured.

Promote extract_date to a keyword-first strategy: first search lines containing DATE / DATED / 'Date :' / 'PRINT DATE' for a date match using DATE_PATTERNS in priority order; only if none are found scan the full text; always prefer the earliest keyed date in reading order, and reject years outside a sensible receipt range (e.g., 2000–2099).

Wire multi_pass_ocr into process_receipt as a retry: if extract_total or extract_date return None, OR if the chosen total disagrees with ≥2 other total-bearing lines (Subtotal+Tax, 'Total Amt Rounded', 'Payment', 'CASH'-'CHANGE') on the same receipt, re-run OCR with alternate PSM/preprocessing variants and re-extract; keep the value that agrees with the most corroborating lines.

Add a short 'receipt field extraction checklist' near the Quality Self-Check section that explicitly calls out: (a) prefer the LAST match in a tier, (b) prefer post-rounding TOTAL, (c) keyword-anchored date, (d) cross-check amount against other total lines, (e) return None (never '', 'nan') on failure.

In the Strict-Schema Outputs section, add an enforced coercion step before to_excel: e.g., `for col in nullable_cols: df[col] = df[col].where(df[col].notna() & (df[col].astype(str).str.len() > 0), None)`, and strengthen the re-read verification to assert that for every row where extraction failed, `pd.isna(cell)` is True (empty cell), not an empty string.

Add a one-line reminder in the canonical pattern that upstream extractors must return Python None (not '', 'None', or NaN) for missing fields, and cite this as the single source of truth so skills like image-ocr and openai-vision align on the same null contract.

observed_failures.evidence: Predictions row for 078.jpg has total_amount="" (empty string) instead of a real null cell. The original image clearly shows 'Grand Total: 92.80', but the agent's extractor returned nothing and the writer serialised that as an empty string, which breaks the task's 'value is set to null' contract and the strict cell-by-cell grader.

For 077.jpg the agent returned 23.26, but the receipt shows two near-duplicate totals ('Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' and a large bold 'TOTAL: 23.25' after a -0.01 rounding adjustment). The feedback marks amount_correct=false, meaning the extractor picked the inclusive-of-GST line instead of the final bold TOTAL that the receipt itself prints last.

For 074.jpg the agent returned 702.00. The receipt plainly prints 'Total Incl. of GST  102.00' three times (Subtotal, Total Incl. of GST, Total Amt Rounded, Payment all = 102.00). The think-trace shows OCR rendered it as 'Total inel. of GBT 702.00' (leading 1 misread as 7). No digit-substitution or cross-line consensus rescue was attempted, so a single OCR glyph error dominated the answer.

For 034.jpg the agent emitted 2018-08-09 but feedback marks date_correct=false. The receipt prints 'Date: 09/03/2018' (DD/MM/YYYY in this Malaysian receipt corpus = 2018-03-09). The extractor appears to have swapped day and month or to have re-ordered a differently printed string, with no rule committing to the DD/MM/YYYY convention that dominates this corpus.

Verifier reward=0.0 while derived field_accuracy=0.909; verifier compares the Excel 'line by line' and any mismatch (including the F1 empty-string vs null cell and F2–F4 wrong values) collapses the whole pass to zero. No field-level partial credit.

root_causes.description: The original image-ocr skill never specifies what to emit when extraction fails, and the original xlsx skill never calls out the strict-schema requirement that missing values be a real null (empty cell), not an empty/'None'/'NaN' string. The agent naturally reached for "" as a sentinel, which the grader sees as a non-matching string.

The original image-ocr skill treats OCR as text extraction only; it has no guidance for 'given multiple TOTAL-bearing lines, which one is THE total'. There is no concept of keyword priority tiers (GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > TOTAL/AMOUNT) and no concept of exclusion keywords (SUBTOTAL/TAX/GST/CHANGE/CASH TENDERED), so the agent re-invented them inconsistently and mis-ranked near-duplicate TOTAL lines like 077.

The original skill shows multi-pass OCR as an optional technique but does not require combining passes or any numeric consensus/plausibility check. Receipts whose totals appear 3–4 times (Subtotal, Total Incl. GST, Total Rounded, Payment) get decided by one noisy glyph. There is no advice to prefer values that recur across lines of the same receipt or across PSM/preprocessing variants.

The original skill never addresses date-format disambiguation. For a Malaysian receipt corpus (RM, SST/GST), DD/MM/YYYY is the dominant convention, but the skill gives no corpus-prior, so the agent can silently pick a MM/DD/YYYY interpretation of the same digits.

The original xlsx skill is oriented at financial models (formulas, formatting) and does not surface the 'graded line-by-line' output contract: exact sheet name, exact column order, no index, no helper columns, string-typed amounts with exactly two decimals, real null cells for missing, lexicographic row order. Without this contract in front of the agent, formatting drift (empty strings, float totals that lose trailing zeros, implicit Sheet1) silently zeroes the reward.

skill_defects.defect: No structured-field extraction section: missing (a) keyword priority tiers, (b) exclusion keyword list, (c) two-line fallback when keyword line has no number, (d) rule that returns None (never '', 'NaN') on failure.

No numeric-robustness guidance: multi-pass OCR is shown but not tied to a 'consensus across passes / across lines of the same receipt' rule, and there is no explicit note that the total of a receipt almost always recurs (Subtotal, Total, Total Rounded, Cash) so disagreement among those candidates is a quality signal.

Date extraction is not covered. No ISO normalisation helper, no ordered format list, and no guidance to commit to the dominant corpus convention (DD/MM/YYYY for RM-denominated receipts) and to return None rather than guess when ambiguous.

No 'strict-schema output' section describing the line-by-line grading contract: exact file path, single named sheet, exact columns/order, index=False, lexicographic filename sort, string-typed amount with two decimals, real nulls for missing. The 'use formulas not hardcoded values' advice is actively misleading for extraction tasks where every cell must be a literal value.

No post-write verification pattern (re-read the file and assert sheet name, column list, row sort, two-decimal string form, real null cells). Agents therefore ship whatever pandas defaulted to (NaN, floats like 47.7, default Sheet1).

repair_recommendations.change: Add a 'Structured Field Extraction (Receipts / Forms)' section that: (1) defines priority tiers as code constants (GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM / TOTAL: RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > NETT TOTAL / TOTAL DUE / AMOUNT DUE / BALANCE DUE / TOTAL / AMOUNT); (2) defines an EXCLUSIONS list (SUBTOTAL, SUB TOTAL, TAX, GST, SST, DISCOUNT, CHANGE, CASH TENDERED) and specifies that exclusion is tested before tier matching; (3) mandates a two-line fallback (if the keyword line has no numeric value, scan the next non-empty, non-excluded line); (4) requires the function to return None (never '', 'None', 'NaN') on failure. Keep this generic — no per-image hard-coding.

In the same section, add tie-breaking guidance when multiple candidates match the same priority tier: prefer the last candidate in reading order (final receipt totals normally print last), but if the final candidate is in a 'GST SUMMARY' / 'TAX SUMMARY' block, exclude the block. This is the generalisable lesson behind the 077 mis-pick.

Add an explicit 'Numeric consensus' subsection: when the same receipt shows a numeric candidate repeated across Subtotal / Total Incl. GST / Total Rounded / Cash / Payment lines, prefer the modal value across these recurrences over a one-off outlier from a single OCR line. Recommend combining a Tesseract multi-pass run (PSM 6 / 4 / 11 on grayscale+autocontrast and inverted variants) and voting on the extracted amount. This generalises beyond 074.

Add a 'Date Extraction and ISO Normalization' subsection with a prioritised regex/format list and a corpus-prior note: for receipts denominated in RM (Malaysian), interpret DD/MM/YYYY (and DD/MM/YY -> 20YY) as the default when the digits are ambiguous; for YYYY-first patterns use them as-is; return None instead of guessing when neither day nor month exceeds 12.

Replace the current 'warnings: [...]' failure examples with a crisp rule: 'On any per-image exception, emit {date: None, total_amount: None} and continue the batch; never emit empty strings, "None", or NaN as field values.' Include a minimal try/except wrapper example.

Add a top-level 'Strict-Schema Outputs (graded line-by-line)' section with a Contract Checklist: (a) write to the exact requested path, (b) exactly one worksheet with the exact requested name (case/spacing), (c) exact column list in exact order with exact headers, (d) index=False and no helper/debug columns, (e) rows sorted as specified (default: lexicographic filename), (f) numeric-looking fields that must be strings written as Python str (e.g. f'{v:.2f}'), not float, (g) missing values written as Python None / pd.NA, never '' / 'None' / 'NaN'. Provide a canonical pandas pattern using ExcelWriter with sheet_name set and df.astype('object') for string columns.

Scope the existing 'Use Formulas, Not Hardcoded Values' guidance to analytical/financial models explicitly, and add a note that strict-schema extraction outputs should contain literal values only (no formulas, no cached-vs-formula mismatch, no recalc dependency).

Add a short 'Post-write verification' snippet: re-open the file with pandas, assert sheet names == expected, assert column list and order, assert row order is lexicographic by the key column, assert every non-null amount matches r'\d+\.\d{2}' and is dtype object, assert null cells read back as NaN (not the string 'nan'). This is the generic safeguard that would have caught 078's empty string before submission.

Add a 'Pitfalls that break line-by-line grading' bullet list: float 47.7 vs string '47.70'; NaN vs None; Sheet1 vs named sheet; index column; thousand separators or currency prefix left in the string; extra confidence/debug columns. Keep this generic — applies to any extraction-to-Excel task.

Add a tiny 'Deterministic batch ordering' note: when the task says 'ordered by filename', enumerate the directory with sorted() on string names (lexicographic), filter by image extensions, and skip hidden files. This reinforces the xlsx row-ordering contract from the OCR side so both skills agree.

confidence.notes: High confidence that F1 (empty string vs null) and F5 (binary reward=0 despite 0.909 field accuracy) are driven by the xlsx strict-schema gap plus the image-ocr failure-mode gap — both are directly observable in the predictions row for 078.jpg and in the delivered file inventory. High confidence that F2/F3 are ranking and single-pass OCR gaps visible in the agent's own think-trace. Medium confidence on F4's exact direction of the DD/MM vs MM/DD error because the oracle date value is not available; the recommendation is written to be safe either way (corpus prior + return None on ambiguity). Recommendations are scoped to the five existing SKILL.md files and avoid any per-receipt hard-coding.

observed_failures.symptom: Month digit misread by OCR; receipt header line is '09/03/2018' but the pipeline committed the August interpretation. Diagnoser visual check of 034 shows date printed as '09/03/2018' in the header near 'Date:' / 'Time:'.

Receipt has several TOTAL-matching lines (Subtotal, Total Excl. of GST 96.23, Total Incl. of GST 102.00, Total Amt Rounded 102.00, Payment 102.00). OCR corrupted the final 'Total Amt Rounded' value to 702.00. Current lowest-tier selector takes the LAST candidate and so returns the corrupted value even though three other TOTAL/AMOUNT lines agree on 102.00.

Receipt has 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26', 'Rounding Adj: -0.01', and a final bold standalone 'TOTAL: 23.25'. Within priority tier 4, the earlier 'Total (Inclusive…)' line was returned instead of the final 'TOTAL:' line, so rounding adjustment was ignored.

Receipt clearly shows 'Grand Total : 92.80' (priority-1 keyword). Nothing was extracted, and the cell was written as an empty string rather than a real null/None. This is simultaneously an extraction miss and a schema-null-handling bug.

root_causes.detail: The guidance in image-ocr says to honor priority tiers and exclusions but is silent about which candidate to pick inside a tier when several lines match. Both 'first match' and 'last match' are wrong in different receipts: for 077 the LAST standalone 'TOTAL:' is the authoritative final value (post-rounding), while for 074 picking the LAST 'Total Amt Rounded' line surfaces an OCR-corrupted number instead of three consistent 102.00 lines. The skill lacks a tie-breaking rule that (a) prefers lines whose keyword is a standalone 'TOTAL' / 'GRAND TOTAL' / 'NET TOTAL' token at line start, and (b) cross-validates against other same-tier candidates when values disagree.

The task hint implies a single final value, but receipts frequently contain both a pre-rounding and a post-rounding total ('Total Rounded', 'Rounded Total (RM):', 'Total Amt Rounded', or a final bold 'TOTAL:' following a 'Rounding Adj' line). The current tiers do not promote the post-rounding/standalone final-TOTAL line above the earlier pre-rounding GST-inclusive subtotal, which caused 077 to miss the 0.01 adjustment.

When extract_total returns None (as happened for 078), the pipeline wrote an empty string into the Excel cell instead of a real null. The xlsx skill documents the 'real null vs "" / "nan"' pitfall only in the candidate draft and only in prose; it does not give an actionable 'build row dict, then astype(object), then let pandas write real empty cells' recipe that an agent will reliably follow. It also does not warn that f-strings, ternaries and pandas default NaN conversion all silently produce string nulls.

Date digits on printed receipts are the single most OCR-fragile tokens (3 vs 8, 0 vs 6, 1 vs 7). The skill shows a multi_pass_ocr pattern for text coverage but does not apply it to date extraction specifically, nor does it combine outputs by voting. 034's '09/03/2018' was misread once as '09/08/2018' and that single hypothesis was committed.

The current NUM_RE accepts thousand-separator and decimal forms but not (a) a bare integer followed by missing decimal (e.g. OCR'd '1000' for '10.00') or (b) comma-as-decimal European style ('20,00'). This is directly implicated in historical '052.jpg GRAND TOTAL 1000' handling and makes the skill brittle on noisy receipts even when the keyword line is correctly identified.

skill_defects.defect: Structured-extraction section defines priority tiers and exclusions but no deterministic intra-tier tie-breaker; no explicit 'prefer standalone TOTAL / rounded-total line that appears AFTER a Rounding Adjustment line' rule.
Date extraction uses first regex match from a single OCR pass; no multi-pass consensus or digit-level sanity check, so a single misread digit silently commits.

Numeric parser does not degrade gracefully when OCR drops the decimal point ('1000' for '10.00') or substitutes a comma ('20,00'); no cross-candidate consistency check when the chosen total disagrees with Subtotal / Cash-Change arithmetic on the same receipt.

process_receipt / per-image pipeline is described as 'returns None on failure' but the skill does not insist that callers write that None through to the final output without intermediate string coercion.

Strict-schema section describes the 'real null vs empty string' pitfall but gives no single tight code recipe binding extractor outputs (Optional[str]) to Excel cells; agents end up writing '' or 'None' when a field is missing (observed in 078.jpg).

No post-write verifier snippet that asserts, for each required column, that every cell is either None (empty) or a str matching the field's exact format (e.g. 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'N.NN'); such a self-check would have caught the 078 empty-string case before submission.

repair_recommendations.change: In the Structured Field Extraction section, add an explicit intra-tier selection rule: within a tier, enumerate ALL non-excluded matches, then pick the candidate using this order: (1) a line whose keyword is a standalone token at line start (e.g. '^\s*TOTAL\b', '^\s*GRAND\s+TOTAL\b', '^\s*NETT?\s+TOTAL\b') that appears AFTER any 'ROUNDING ADJ' / 'ROUND(ED)?' line in the text, (2) otherwise the line with a '^\s*TOTAL\b' standalone token, (3) otherwise the LAST non-excluded match. Document that this implements the 'final total after rounding' convention common on Malaysian receipts.

Add a cross-candidate consistency check: after choosing a tier winner, if the selected numeric value disagrees with the MAJORITY value among the other non-excluded same-tier candidates by more than a cent, and the majority value is present in >= 2 other lines, prefer the majority value. This rescues 074-style single-line OCR corruptions while leaving well-formed receipts unchanged.

Promote 'ROUNDED TOTAL', 'TOTAL ROUNDED', 'TOTAL AMT ROUNDED', 'ROUNDED TOTAL (RM)' and standalone final 'TOTAL:' / 'TOTAL RM:' patterns into a new tier that sits ABOVE the generic 'TOTAL / AMOUNT' tier, so the post-rounding final value wins over earlier GST-inclusive subtotals. Keep 'GRAND TOTAL' and 'TOTAL (:) RM' at their current top positions.

In Date Extraction, replace the single-pass single-match pattern with a multi-hypothesis strategy: run date regex over text produced by at least 2 preprocessing variants (grayscale+autocontrast, inverted, upscale 2x) and at least 2 PSM modes (6 and 11); collect candidates, canonicalize each to ISO; if multiple distinct ISO candidates exist, prefer the one appearing in the greatest number of passes (majority vote), breaking ties by earliest reading-order position. Return None when no pass yields a valid date.

Widen numeric handling: (a) allow a dot-missing fallback where a keyword-line integer is interpreted as 'X.XX' only when its length is >= 3 AND the surrounding tier's other candidates agree on that magnitude; (b) accept 'NN,NN' as decimal when no three-digit thousand group follows; (c) always strip leading currency tokens ('RM', '$', 'MYR') before conversion; (d) format outputs as f"{v:.2f}" strings. Document each branch with a one-line example.

Expand EXCLUSIONS with task-observed noise lines that leaked into totals in prior runs: 'TOTAL ITEMS', 'TOTAL QTY', 'TOTAL QUANTITY', 'TOTAL SAVINGS', 'ITEM COUNT', 'AVERAGE / PAX', 'AMOUNT(RM) TAX', and section headers 'GST SUMMARY' / 'TAX SUMMARY' (and ignore all lines after such a header when extracting totals).

In Per-Image Pipeline, state as a hard contract: process_receipt MUST return a dict whose values are either a correctly-formatted str (date 'YYYY-MM-DD' or amount 'N.NN') or Python None — never '', 'None', 'nan', 0, or a float. Any downstream writer must propagate None untouched.

In Strict-Schema Outputs, replace the current prose checklist with a copy-pasteable end-to-end recipe: build list-of-dicts with None for missing fields, construct DataFrame with explicit columns, df = df.astype({col: 'object' for col in required_cols}), df.sort_values('filename', kind='stable'), then pd.ExcelWriter(..., engine='openpyxl') to_excel(sheet_name='<exact>', index=False, na_rep=''). Explicitly warn: do NOT use df.fillna(''), do NOT use f-strings to coerce None, do NOT rely on pandas' default NaN -> blank behaviour (it works, but only if dtype stays object).

Add a mandatory post-write verifier template: re-open the written file with openpyxl (data_only=True), assert sheet names == required, header row == required columns, every data row's missing fields are Python None (cell.value is None), every present amount matches r'^\d+\.\d{2}$', every present date matches r'^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$', and rows are sorted ascending by filename. Fail loudly if any assertion breaks before the task is considered finished.

Add a short 'Null vs Empty String: Observed Failure Mode' note citing the generic pattern (OCR pipeline returns None, agent writes '' via an f-string or a ternary that coerces None to ''), with a one-line fix pattern: `value = fields['total_amount'] if fields['total_amount'] is not None else None` — never `str(fields['total_amount'] or '')`.

confidence.notes: Four failing cells are directly inspectable in the supplied receipt images and cleanly map to either a tier-selection rule (074, 077), a date-OCR single-pass weakness (034), or a null-handling bug in the Excel writer (078). Recommendations stay within the five existing SKILL.md files and generalize beyond these 22 receipts (post-rounding final-TOTAL precedence, multi-pass date voting, strict null propagation). Residual uncertainty concerns (a) whether the cross-candidate majority rule could occasionally override a correctly OCR'd final-rounded total that legitimately differs by rounding from pre-rounding candidates — mitigated by requiring >= 2 agreeing other lines and a > 0.01 gap; and (b) whether the oracle for 077 truly expects the post-rounding 23.25 — which the receipt image strongly supports but cannot be verified from permitted feedback alone.

observed_failures.symptom: Agent took last candidate on a keyword line where OCR mangled '102.00' into '702.00' ('1' confused with '7'); no consensus with repeated 102.00 elsewhere on receipt.

observed_failures.symptom: Priority tier matched 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' before the bold rounded 'TOTAL' line; the final rounded TOTAL (23.25) was ignored.

root_causes: image-ocr priority tiers conflate 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' and 'Rounded TOTAL': both match the generic TOTAL tier, and the current rule 'prefer earliest' or 'prefer a specific tier' picks the pre-rounding value when the final TOTAL appears later.

Amount extraction relies on a single OCR candidate per line with no cross-check against other high-signal lines on the same receipt (subtotal, cash, payment, rounded total). OCR digit confusions (1/7, 0/O, 8/3) therefore propagate directly to the output.
Date extraction runs on a single OCR pass with no voting across preprocessing variants; a single mis-OCR'd digit silently produces a wrong but parseable ISO date.

The output writer does not enforce None-vs-empty-string: when per-field extraction returned None the agent wrote '' into the cell, which is scored as incorrect and is explicitly warned against in the current xlsx skill but not enforced via a verification step.
Fallback 'last number on keyword line' has no sanity filter: it will accept a heavily mangled number ('——S«702.00') that disagrees with other copies of the same amount elsewhere on the receipt.

skill_defects.defect: TOTAL_PRIORITY tiers do not include an explicit 'rounded/final total' tier (e.g., 'TOTAL AFTER ROUNDING', 'TOTAL ROUNDED', 'ROUNDED TOTAL', 'GRAND TOTAL' after a rounding-adjustment line) above the generic 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' / 'Net Total' matches.

extract_total selects a single candidate without any within-receipt corroboration. There is no guidance to collect all monetary candidates with 2 decimals and prefer the value that is repeated (e.g., Subtotal == Total == Payment).

Multi-pass OCR pattern is described but not applied to structured extraction: the skill does not say 'run both default-PSM and preprocessed OCR, extract (tier, value) from each, and vote', which is the exact pattern needed for OCR digit-confusion cases.

Date extraction section does not require cross-pass agreement and does not note that DD/MM vs MM/DD ambiguity plus single-digit OCR errors (e.g., '03'→'08') must be defended against by voting across passes or by preferring dates that also appear in a secondary location on the receipt.

Strict-Schema Outputs section warns against empty strings but provides no concrete pre-write normalization step (e.g., replace '', 'None', 'NaN', 'nan' with None) and no post-write assertion that empty cells are truly empty, not ''. The failure on 078.jpg is exactly this pattern.

No guidance that extraction-pipeline None values must bubble through pandas without being coerced to NaN strings when writing via ExcelWriter; the canonical pattern does not include a `df.where(df.notna(), None)` or equivalent safety net.

repair_recommendations.change: Introduce a top-priority tier for post-rounding/final totals that must be tried before generic 'TOTAL'/'AMOUNT' matches: patterns like r'TOTAL\s*(AFTER\s*)?ROUND(ED|ING)?', r'ROUNDED\s*TOTAL', r'TOTAL\s*AMT\s*ROUNDED', and prefer the LAST occurrence of 'TOTAL' when a 'ROUNDING ADJ' line appears above it. Document that on receipts with both 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' and a later bold 'TOTAL' the later one wins.

Add a 'within-receipt corroboration' step for total extraction: collect every candidate line's (tier, value) across ALL keyword matches (including payment/cash/rounded-total/subtotal) and, when the top tier yields a value that does NOT appear anywhere else in the receipt text, prefer a tied-or-lower-tier value that is repeated at least twice. This defends against single-line OCR digit errors (1/7, 0/8).

Promote the existing multi-pass OCR pattern from a nice-to-have into the documented pipeline for structured receipt extraction: run default PSM and preprocessed+PSM6 passes, extract (tier, value) from each, prefer higher-priority tier; on tier tie, prefer agreement; on disagreement with equal priority, prefer the candidate that has exactly 2 decimal digits and appears elsewhere on the receipt. Include a short pseudocode block, not a full implementation.

Harden date extraction: require at least one of (a) the same ISO date to parse from two OCR variants, or (b) the day/month/year to each individually appear in >=2 passes. If no corroboration is possible, prefer returning None over a single-pass guess. Add explicit note that DD/MM/YYYY is the default ordering for the receipt domain and MM/DD/YYYY must not be attempted first.

Expand the number regex guidance: monetary totals MUST have exactly 2 decimal digits (reject 'XX.X' and bare integers) and must not be preceded/followed by a digit. Explicitly warn that candidates with adjacent OCR noise (non-ascii, consecutive punctuation like '——S«', trailing letters) should be down-weighted or skipped when a cleaner candidate of equal priority exists.

Add a required pre-write normalization step to the Strict-Schema Outputs canonical pattern: convert '', 'None', 'none', 'NaN', 'nan', and pandas NA to Python None for every cell before `to_excel`, e.g. `df = df.where(pd.notna(df), None); df = df.replace({'': None, 'None': None, 'NaN': None, 'nan': None})`. Make this step MANDATORY, not optional, and show it in the canonical snippet.

Add a post-write verification assertion that for every column the set of 'missing' cells is exactly those where the source row had None; specifically, re-open the file and assert that no cell contains the string '' or 'nan'. Include this in the verification checklist and in the canonical example.

Clarify that when a per-row processing function returns None for a field, callers MUST propagate None end-to-end (not '' or 'null' or 'N/A'). Add this as a bullet in the Pitfalls list referencing the extraction-row pattern already shown in image-ocr.

observed_failures.observation: Predicted 702.00 while receipt visibly shows 102.00 for Subtotal, Total incl. of GST, Total Amt Rounded, and Payment. OCR misread leading '1' as '7' on at least one line, and extractor picked the misread value.

Predicted 23.26 but receipt's bolded final line is 'TOTAL: 23.25' after a -0.01 rounding adjustment. Extractor picked the pre-rounding 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' instead of the final rounded 'TOTAL' line.

Predicted empty string ("") rather than a value or real null. Receipt is a Thai Delicious Restaurant bill whose final line is 'Grand Total: 92.80'; extractor failed and also emitted an empty string instead of None, which is a schema-violating value for a missing field.

Predicted 2018-08-09 but receipt date field reads 'Date: 09/03/2018' (DD/MM/YYYY → 2018-03-09). The extractor appears to have parsed 09/03/2018 as MM/DD/YYYY, producing month=8 via a different candidate or a format-order bug.

Run terminated at max_iterations (65) with acp_stop_reason=max_turn_requests; Agent spent many iterations hand-tuning OCR variants per image rather than converging on a generalizable rule, indicating the Skill did not give it a stable recipe for receipt-field extraction.

root_causes.summary: image-ocr Skill lacks a receipt-specific field-extraction recipe
root_causes.detail: The original image-ocr SKILL.md documents Tesseract usage and multi-pass OCR but gives no priority/exclusion rules for TOTAL keywords, no two-line fallback, no amount normalization to a 2-decimal string, and no date normalization to ISO. The Agent had to invent all of this from scratch inside the task loop, which is why 65 iterations were consumed and why edge cases (rounded total vs. inclusive total, DD/MM vs MM/DD, OCR digit confusions) were handled ad-hoc.

root_causes.summary: No guidance to prefer the final/rounded total over pre-rounding or pre-tax 'Total' lines
root_causes.detail: The task's priority list treats plain 'TOTAL' as a single tier. Real receipts routinely contain multiple 'Total' lines — 'Total (Inclusive of GST)', 'Total incl. of GST', 'Total Rounded', 'Total Amt Rounded', 'Rounding Adj', final 'TOTAL'. Without a rule that says 'when several TOTAL-tier lines exist, prefer the last one that is the rounded/net final total (keywords ROUNDED, NET, GRAND, or the line immediately before CASH/CHANGE)', the extractor cannot reliably pick 23.25 over 23.26 or 102.00 over a misread 702.00.

root_causes.summary: Ambiguous date formats are not disambiguated by receipt locale cues
root_causes.detail: Receipts in this dataset are Malaysian and overwhelmingly DD/MM/YYYY. The Agent's DATE_PATTERNS list includes both %d/%m/%Y and %Y/%m/%d but no %m/%d/%Y; however it appears to have accepted a day>12 interpretation that still produced a wrong month for 034.jpg. The Skill gives no rule like 'treat dd/mm/yyyy as the default when the receipt is Malaysian/UK-style, and only fall back to mm/dd/yyyy if the first field is > 12'.

root_causes.summary: xlsx Skill does not forbid empty strings for missing fields
root_causes.detail: For 078.jpg the Agent wrote total_amount = "" instead of a real null. The task spec says 'the value is set to null' on failure, and the grader treats "" as different from None. The original xlsx SKILL.md focuses on formulas/formatting and has no 'strict-schema extraction output' section telling the Agent to use Python None (empty cell), avoid NaN strings, write amounts as 2-decimal strings, and sort lexicographically by filename.

root_causes.summary: No OCR-robustness rule for digit confusions on the TOTAL line
root_causes.detail: '102.00' vs '702.00' and '0' vs '6' confusions are the dominant OCR errors on these scans. The Skill does not tell the Agent to (a) run multiple OCR variants and take the majority value among candidates matching the same keyword, (b) cross-check TOTAL against Subtotal / Payment / Cash-Change arithmetic (total = cash - change) as a tiebreaker, or (c) prefer the TOTAL value that equals the Payment line on the same receipt.

root_causes.summary: Agent-loop budget was consumed by per-image debugging
root_causes.detail: Iteration accounting shows 65 iterations hit the cap; many were spent re-running OCR with different PSM/preprocess variants on single images. The Skills do not prescribe a 'do multi-pass OCR once, extract with the rule set, move on' pipeline, so the Agent kept entering local debugging loops.

skill_defects.defect: Missing a documented receipt-field extraction recipe: no TOTAL_PRIORITY tiers, no EXCLUSION list, no two-line fallback, no amount normalization to a 2-decimal string, no ISO date normalization, no per-image try/except that degrades to None.
No guidance on disambiguating multiple TOTAL-like lines on the same receipt (Rounded vs Inclusive vs Excluding vs Subtotal), and no rule to prefer the final/rounded total nearest to CASH/CHANGE.
No locale/format guidance for dates: DD/MM/YYYY default, fallback to MM/DD/YYYY only if day>12, reject impossible months, try both orderings before returning None.

No OCR-robustness strategy for noisy digits on the TOTAL line: no cross-validation with Subtotal/Payment/Cash-Change, no majority vote across OCR variants, no acceptance criterion based on 2-decimal-place numeric shape.

No 'strict-schema extraction output' section: nothing tells the Agent to write real nulls (Python None) for missing fields, to write monetary totals as 2-decimal strings (not floats), to use sheet_name='results' with index=False, to sort lexicographically by filename, and to verify by re-reading. The Skill's existing emphasis on formulas is irrelevant and distracting for this task.
No explicit warning that empty string, 'nan', 'None', and NaN are all distinct from None and will fail line-by-line grading.

For tasks where a receipt is scanned with heavy OCR noise, there is no cross-reference from image-ocr pointing to vision-based OCR as a fallback for low-confidence Tesseract results. Not a blocking defect for the current pass/fail but relevant for generalization.
No defect observed for this task; the input is JPG, not PDF.
No defect observed for this task; the input is static images, not video.

repair_recommendations.change: Add a 'Structured Field Extraction (Receipts / Forms)' section that documents a tiered TOTAL_PRIORITY list (GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM / TOTAL: RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > NETT/NET TOTAL / TOTAL DUE / AMOUNT DUE / BALANCE DUE / bare TOTAL / AMOUNT) and an EXCLUSIONS list (SUBTOTAL, SUB TOTAL, TAX, GST, SST, DISCOUNT, CHANGE, CASH TENDERED, EXCLUDING, EXCL., TOTAL ITEMS/QTY/SAVINGS). Exclusions must be checked before keyword matching. Keep this generic enough to apply to any priority/exclusion task.

Specify a 'pick the final total when multiple TOTAL-tier candidates exist' rule: among candidates in the same tier, prefer the one that (a) appears closest to CASH/PAYMENT/CHANGE lines, (b) contains ROUNDED/NET/GRAND/FINAL, or (c) agrees with the Payment line value. Also add a two-line fallback: if the keyword line has no numeric value, use the last number on the next non-empty line.

Document amount normalization: strip currency prefixes (RM, $, €), strip thousand separators, require exactly two decimal places via f"{value:.2f}", and return a Python str. Document date normalization: try DD/MM/YYYY first, then DD-MM-YYYY, then YYYY-MM-DD, then DD MMM YYYY, DD-MMM-YYYY, DD/MM/YY; reject any match whose month>12 or day>31; return datetime.date.isoformat() or None.

Document an OCR-robustness strategy: run multi_pass_ocr with several PSM modes and preprocessing variants (grayscale+autocontrast, invert, 2x upscale, sharpen), collect all candidates per tier from all passes, and resolve conflicts by majority vote; on tie, prefer the candidate equal to the Payment/Cash-minus-Change arithmetic check.

Mandate per-image try/except that always returns {date, total_amount} with None for any field that cannot be extracted; never raise out of the per-image function and never return empty strings. Add a 'Quality Self-Check' bullet list enforcing these invariants.

Add a 'Strict-Schema Outputs (graded line-by-line)' section with an explicit checklist: exact file path, exactly one sheet with the exact name (e.g., 'results'), exact column names in exact order, no index column (index=False), deterministic lexicographic sort by filename, and a verification step that re-reads the file and asserts shape/columns/sheet name.

Document that missing/unparseable values MUST be Python None (empty cell), not '', 'None', 'NaN', or nan. Document that monetary totals formatted like '47.70' MUST be written as Python str (not float) and show the pattern of forcing dtype='object' before to_excel. Keep the formula/formatting guidance but clearly scope it to analytical models, not extraction outputs.

Add a short canonical pattern for 'list-of-dicts → DataFrame with explicit columns → to_excel(sheet_name=..., index=False) → re-read and assert' that generalizes to any similar extraction-to-spreadsheet task.

Add a brief cross-reference: when Tesseract OCR confidence is low or key fields (date/total) cannot be extracted deterministically, fall back to vision-based OCR with a strict JSON schema prompt that asks only for the needed fields, and feed the result back through the same normalization rules defined in image-ocr.
No change required for this task; keep the Skill as-is.
