root_causes: image-ocr skill's receipt field extractor leaves the 'pick among same-tier candidates' rule ambiguous: current draft uses first match within a tier, but final totals on Malaysian receipts often appear AFTER a rounding-adjustment line; the extractor must prefer the LAST same-tier match below any 'Rounding Adj'/'Total After Rounding' line, not the first.

image-ocr skill recommends multi-pass OCR but does not require voting/consensus or sanity bounds on extracted numbers; a single corrupt pass can produce impossible values (e.g. 702.00 when all visible totals are ~92.80).

image-ocr skill's date extractor iterates DATE_PATTERNS in a fixed list order and returns the first regex hit anywhere in the text, with no preference for a date that appears on a line containing a 'Date'/'Tarikh'/'Invoice Date' label; it also has no tie-break when both %d/%m/%Y and %m/%d/%Y could parse.

xlsx skill describes null-vs-empty handling but the per-image pipeline example returns strings and the writing example does not force None/pd.NA conversion before to_excel; the agent produced an empty string for 078 instead of a true null cell.

No skill instructs the agent to cap work-per-image and fall through to null when confidence is low, so the agent burned the 65-iteration budget debugging individual images instead of hardening the shared pipeline.

skill_defects.defect: extract_total chooses first same-tier match; needs explicit 'prefer the last same-tier candidate, and if a 'Rounding Adj'/'Total After Rounding'/'Rounded Total' line exists, prefer the total that follows it' rule.

No consensus/voting procedure across OCR variants, and no sanity filter (e.g., reject totals that differ by >5x from any other same-tier candidate across variants, or that exceed a reasonable receipt bound).

extract_date has no label-proximity preference and no locale hint. Should: (1) first scan lines containing 'Date'/'Tarikh'/'Invoice Date'/'Inv Date' and extract from those; (2) default to day-first (DD/MM) for ambiguous numeric dates typical of Malaysian/SG/UK receipts; (3) reject dates outside a plausible window.
No per-image iteration budget or 'return (None, None) on low confidence' guidance; encourages open-ended retries that can exhaust the agent loop.

Strict-schema section shows the pattern but does not forbid writing '' for missing values nor require a final normalization pass that converts '', 'nan', 'None', NaN → None before to_excel. The 078 failure traces directly to this gap.
Verification checklist does not include an assertion that empty/missing cells read back as NaN/None (not the string 'nan' or ''); needs an explicit post-write check.

repair_recommendations.change: In the Structured Field Extraction section, replace the 'try candidates from first match' behavior with: within a tier, collect all non-excluded matches; if the text contains a 'ROUNDING ADJ', 'TOTAL AFTER ROUNDING', or 'ROUNDED TOTAL' line, prefer the last match that appears at or after that line; otherwise prefer the last match in reading order. Document this rule explicitly with a worked example.

Add a 'Multi-Variant Consensus' subsection: run OCR on at least {default, autocontrast+PSM6, 2x-upscaled+PSM6} variants; for each variant compute (tier, value); pick the value that (a) comes from the highest-priority tier observed across variants, then (b) has the most variant votes, then (c) comes from the latest line. Provide the pick_best_total helper in the skill text.

Add a numeric sanity filter: reject any candidate total that is >10x the median of other same-tier candidates across variants, and reject totals outside (0.01, 1_000_000); on rejection fall back to the next candidate, and if none remain emit None.

Rewrite extract_date to: (1) first search only lines whose upper-cased text contains 'DATE', 'TARIKH', 'INV DATE', or 'INVOICE DATE' (and not 'PRINT DATE'/'CLOSE'); (2) only if none found, fall back to a full-text scan; (3) for ambiguous NN/NN/NNNN strings, parse as day-first by default and document the override hook; (4) clamp to a plausible year range (e.g., 2000-2099) and return None otherwise.

Add a 'Per-Image Budget' note: cap OCR variants to a small fixed set (3–5); on any exception or if all variants fail to produce a tiered match, return (None, None) rather than looping. State explicitly that null is the correct output when extraction is uncertain.

In the Strict-Schema Outputs canonical pattern, add a final normalization step before to_excel: df = df.replace({'': None, 'nan': None, 'NaN': None, 'None': None}); df = df.where(pd.notna(df), None); and explicitly state 'Never write empty strings — they are indistinguishable from real values to some graders.'

Extend the post-write verification snippet to assert that cells expected to be null read back as NaN/None, e.g. assert check['results'].isna().sum().sum() == expected_null_count or at minimum assert no cell equals '' or the literal string 'nan'.
In Pitfalls, add a bullet: 'Writing "" for a failed extraction — always coerce to None/pd.NA before to_excel so the cell is truly empty.'

The 074 hallucination (702.00) is diagnosed indirectly from the image + predicted value since no raw OCR text is in this window; the voting+sanity-bound remedy generalizes beyond the specific token. Root-cause for 034 (date) is likely-but-not-certain label-proximity vs day-first parsing — both repairs are defensive and compatible.

root_causes.summary: Date parser misinterprets DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY
root_causes.detail: DATE_PATTERNS tries %d/%m/%Y first but fallback or alternative orderings can still match earlier regex when strings like '09/03/2018' appear; no locale hint or rejection of impossible day>12 disambiguation leading to swapped month/day for cases like 034.jpg.

root_causes.summary: Total selector does not prefer the LAST matching priority line
root_causes.detail: When multiple lines satisfy the same priority tier (e.g., 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' followed by 'TOTAL: 23.25' after rounding), algorithm returns the first match in reading order. For receipts with rounding adjustments the final printed total is the last tier-matching line, not the first.

root_causes.summary: Fallback to last-number-on-next-line mis-triggers on payment lines
root_causes.detail: When the keyword line has no numeric value (e.g., OCR lost it), the next-line fallback can pick a non-total line (change/visa/cash) if exclusion check isn't applied to the fallback line or if OCR text differs from the exclusion vocabulary (e.g., 'Visa', 'Cash Received'). 074.jpg's 702.00 and 078.jpg behaviour are consistent with this.

root_causes.summary: Missing/unparseable values written as empty string, not real null
root_causes.detail: 078.jpg total_amount is '' rather than an empty (None) cell. The writer path does not convert '' -> None before to_excel, violating the strict-schema contract.

root_causes.summary: Exclusion keyword list is incomplete/narrow
root_causes.detail: EXCLUSIONS covers SUBTOTAL/TAX/GST/SST/DISCOUNT/CHANGE/CASH TENDERED but misses payment-method lines (VISA, MASTERCARD, DEBIT, CARD, PAYMENT, CASH RECEIVED, AMOUNT TENDERED, CHANGE DUE, TOTAL GROSS when it duplicates fuel total, AVERAGE/PAX) and totals-adjacent noise (ROUNDING ADJ, ROUNDED TOTAL vs TOTAL ROUNDED ambiguity). Allows wrong candidate lines to be selected or wrong fallback.

skill_defects.defect: Priority/exclusion algorithm picks first matching line per tier instead of the LAST matching line within the same tier; two-line fallback does not re-check exclusions on the fallback line.

Exclusion vocabulary is too small for Malaysian receipts: missing VISA, MASTERCARD, DEBIT, CARD, PAYMENT, CASH, CASH RECEIVED, AMOUNT TENDERED, CHANGE DUE, ROUNDING, ROUND(ED) ADJ, TOTAL GROSS (for fuel receipts where it duplicates Total), AVERAGE/PAX.

extract_date returns first regex match without disambiguating ambiguous numeric date formats; no sanity check (day<=12 vs >12), and no preference for a date appearing near 'Date:' label vs other numeric strings; multi-pass OCR text concatenation can surface a different date (e.g., print time) ahead of the real purchase date.
Receipts with 'Rounding Adj' followed by a second 'TOTAL' line (post-rounding) are not handled — algorithm does not know that the final printed total supersedes earlier tier matches.
No vote/aggregation across multi-pass OCR variants: variants disagree (e.g., 23.25 vs 23.26) and the pipeline keeps the first variant's answer rather than the majority value.

Strict-schema writer accepts empty strings in the output DataFrame; does not coerce '' / 'None' / 'NaN' / 'nan' to real None before to_excel, producing non-null cells where the contract requires empty cells.
No post-write verification that every total_amount string matches /^\d+\.\d{2}$/ and every date matches /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ or is empty; this would have caught the 078.jpg '' before submission.

repair_recommendations.change: In structured total extraction, within each priority tier collect ALL matching lines and return the LAST one (bottom-most) that passes exclusions; only fall through to lower tiers if no tier-N line yields a parseable number. This handles rounding-adjusted receipts where the final printed TOTAL is below an earlier tier match.

Re-apply the exclusion check to the fallback (next) line used when a keyword line lacks a number. Skip the fallback (and try the line after) if the candidate line contains any exclusion token, and never accept a fallback number from a line whose keyword itself is a payment/tender/change indicator.

Expand EXCLUSIONS to include payment/tender/change/rounding terms common on receipts: VISA, MASTERCARD, DEBIT, CARD, PAYMENT, CASH, CASH RECEIVED, AMOUNT TENDERED, CHANGE DUE, ROUNDING, ROUND ADJ, ROUNDING ADJ, ROUNDING ADJUSTMENT, TOTAL GROSS (fuel receipts), AVERAGE, PAX, ITEM COUNT, QTY, POINTS, SAVINGS. Also treat 'TOTAL GROSS' and 'TOTAL EXCL GST' as exclusions when a plain 'TOTAL' line exists.

Add a majority-vote aggregator across OCR preprocessing variants: run extract_total on each variant, then return the modal string value; ties broken by (a) highest-priority tier that produced it, (b) variant with highest average OCR confidence. Same voting for extract_date.

Make extract_date prefer a match that occurs on or immediately after a line containing 'DATE', 'TARIKH', 'INVOICE DATE', or 'RECEIPT DATE'. If multiple candidates exist, prefer the one closest in text to such a label; otherwise use the earliest match. Add a sanity check: if day>12 and month>12 both appear possible, prefer DD/MM for Malaysian/EU receipts (document this assumption).

Document a two-line keyword/value handling rule: when a keyword line (TOTAL, GRAND TOTAL, AMOUNT DUE) has no numeric and the next line has only a number, require that the number be formatted as N.NN (two decimals) and not be preceded by a currency-less integer alone (to avoid picking item counts).

Add a self-check step: parsed total_amount must satisfy regex ^\d+\.\d{2}$ with value in a plausible receipt range (0.10–100000.00); otherwise return None. Parsed date must satisfy ^(20\d{2})-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$; otherwise return None.

In the strict-schema writer, after building the DataFrame, replace '', 'None', 'NaN', 'nan', numpy.nan in the output columns with Python None (e.g., df = df.where(df.astype(str).apply(lambda s: s.str.strip()).ne('').where(lambda x: x, other=False), None) or df.replace({'': None, 'None': None, 'NaN': None, 'nan': None}) and then astype('object')).

Add a mandatory post-write verification block for extraction tasks: re-read the xlsx, assert exactly one sheet with the required name, assert exact column order and header text, assert row count equals input count, assert lexicographic filename ordering, and assert each non-null total_amount matches ^\d+\.\d{2}$ and each non-null date matches ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$. Fail loudly if any check fails so the agent fixes before finishing.

Document that for graded extraction outputs, every cell must be a literal string or a real null; never write Python floats or format-dependent values, and never leave helper columns like confidence/raw_text in the final sheet.

Add explicit guidance and example code for 'final printed total supersedes earlier pre-rounding total' — i.e., search for a 'ROUNDING' or 'ROUND(ED) ADJ' line and, if present, prefer a TOTAL/GRAND TOTAL/NET TOTAL line that appears AFTER it over any earlier total match.

Add guidance that for fuel receipts, 'Total Gross' is typically a duplicate of 'Total' and should be excluded from candidate selection when a plain 'Total RM <value>' line is present; pick the plain Total line.

root_causes.summary: Output serialization in the current xlsx guidance does not force None for failed-extraction cells. Even the draft xlsx SKILL mentions it but the original run clearly produced ""; pandas default for missing strings in an object column becomes NaN or "" depending on build path, and there is no explicit sanitization step before to_excel().

Total-extraction logic in image-ocr SKILL is keyword-first but not 'final-total-line last'. Receipts frequently repeat TOTAL (pre-tax / incl-GST / post-rounding). The priority tiers resolve the keyword but not the temporal 'last authoritative TOTAL after rounding' rule, which is what graders encode.

Multi-variant OCR voting is per-tier majority on extracted values only; it does not use repeated-number consensus from the full OCR text. On digit confusions like 1↔7, the correct value is often present multiple times elsewhere (Subtotal, Payment, Total Rounded) and that structural redundancy is thrown away.

Exclusion list under-specified: covers 'CASH TENDERED' but not other cash-side labels ('CASH RECEIVED', 'CASH PAYMENT', 'CASH', 'VISA', 'MASTERCARD', 'CARD', 'PAID', 'TENDER'). Two-line fallback then latches onto payment-method lines whose amounts are often >= total.

Date extraction lacks locale/convention bias. For Malaysian receipts (the obvious domain of these samples: RM, GST, SST), DD/MM/YYYY should outrank MM/DD/YYYY when both parse. There is also no cross-variant voting on the date; a single OCR mis-read on one variant can change the winner.

No 'budget-aware' plan: the method rewrites and re-runs the whole batch on every tweak instead of caching per-image OCR text and only re-running the field extractor, so iteration budget is burned on re-OCR rather than on logic fixes.

defects: Priority tiers do not specify 'prefer the LAST matching line within the highest priority tier', which is the empirical rule for post-rounding final totals.
Two-line fallback is unguarded: it fires whenever the keyword line has no digits, even if the next line is a payment-method/card/cash line.
Exclusion list missing CASH RECEIVED, CASH PAYMENT, CASH, VISA, MASTERCARD, CARD, PAID, TENDER, ROUNDING, ROUNDING ADJ (the adjustment amount itself is not the total).
No cross-variant consensus that leverages repetition of the same numeric value elsewhere in the text (Subtotal == Total == Payment is strong evidence against an outlier OCR read).
Date extraction has no explicit 'prefer DD/MM/YYYY when ambiguous' toggle for Malaysian-style receipts, no voting across OCR variants, and no sanity check (year in a plausible range).
No explicit statement that final output values must be returned as None (not '', not 'None', not NaN) when extraction fails.

Strict-schema section mentions None vs '' but does not prescribe a mandatory sanitization pass (e.g., df.replace({'': None, 'nan': None, 'None': None}) and df.where(df.notna(), None)) immediately before to_excel().
No prescribed post-write re-read-and-assert step that verifies empty cells are truly empty (not "") and that all amounts are strings matching r'^\d+\.\d{2}$' or null.
No guidance on sheet-name casing: the task fixes 'results' (lowercase). The checklist mentions it but should elevate to a required assertion before closing the writer.

No pattern for using vision as a low-cost rescue step for a small residual set (the N receipts where Tesseract produced ambiguous results). The source run never invoked vision even when stuck on ~2 images for many iterations.

Not materially implicated by this task; however, since receipts sometimes arrive as scanned PDFs, cross-reference to image-ocr's structured-field extraction is missing (a one-line pointer would make the batch pipeline reusable).
Not implicated by this task.

repair_recommendations.change: Add an explicit 'Receipt Total Selection Rules' subsection that codifies: (a) within the highest-priority tier that has any match, prefer the LAST matching line (bottom-of-receipt wins) over the first; (b) when the chosen line's extracted number differs from a number that appears >=2 times elsewhere in the OCR text (e.g., Subtotal, Payment, Total Rounded), prefer the repeated value — this neutralizes 1↔7, 0↔8, 3↔5 digit confusions.

Expand EXCLUSIONS to include: SUBTOTAL, SUB TOTAL, TAX, GST, SST, DISCOUNT, CHANGE, CASH, CASH TENDERED, CASH RECEIVED, CASH PAYMENT, VISA, MASTERCARD, MASTER CARD, CARD, DEBIT, CREDIT, PAID, TENDER, TENDERED, ROUNDING, ROUNDING ADJ, ADJUSTMENT. Match as word-boundary regex, case-insensitive. Apply exclusions to BOTH the keyword line and any two-line-fallback next line.

Guard the two-line fallback: only descend to the next line if the keyword line has no digits AND the next non-empty line passes exclusion AND the next line's value is not larger than the largest numeric already seen with a 'SUBTOTAL' or 'TOTAL' keyword (this blocks CASH 100.00 from capturing a 92.80 total).

Add a structured date-selection subsection: (a) run DATE_PATTERNS on every OCR variant; (b) when both DD/MM/YYYY and MM/DD/YYYY parse the same token, prefer DD/MM/YYYY (receipts in this domain are consistently DD/MM); (c) vote across variants and pick the ISO date with the highest frequency, tiebreaking by earliest-in-reading-order; (d) reject years outside a configurable sanity range (default 2000–2099).
State the output contract for structured extraction explicitly: on failure, return Python None for every field, never '', 'None', or NaN. Downstream callers MUST propagate None unchanged.

Document a caching recipe: run multi_pass_ocr once per image and persist the raw text (e.g., to a JSON sidecar keyed by filename+md5). Re-runs of the field extractor should read the cache instead of re-OCRing — this is what makes iterative repair feasible within turn budgets.

Promote the strict-schema sanitization to a required pre-write step with explicit code: coerce the output DataFrame with df = df.astype(object).where(df.notna(), None); then df.replace({'': None, 'nan': None, 'NaN': None, 'None': None}, inplace=True); then to_excel(..., sheet_name=<exact name>, index=False). Make this the canonical pattern in the 'Strict-Schema Outputs' section.

Require a post-write verification block that re-reads the file with openpyxl (not pandas, to see true cell type) and asserts: (a) exactly one sheet with the exact required name (case-sensitive); (b) header row equals the required columns in order; (c) for every numeric-looking string column, each non-null cell matches a regex (e.g., r'^\d+(?:\.\d{2})?$' for amounts formatted to 2 decimals); (d) blank-missing cells are truly empty (cell.value is None), not the literal strings '' / 'None' / 'nan'.
Add a short 'string-vs-float amount pitfall' callout: amounts specified as '47.70' must be written as Python str; using float will drop the trailing zero and change the cell type, failing graders.

Add a 'Residual-Rescue Pattern' subsection: when a batch OCR pipeline leaves <= K images with low confidence or unresolved key fields, invoke GPT-4o vision with detail='high' on just those images, with a tightly-scoped prompt asking for ONLY {date, total_amount} as JSON. This bounds cost while recovering the long tail. Include a token budget estimate and a reminder that vision output must also be sanitized to None on failure.

Add a single cross-reference line to image-ocr's structured-field extraction section, noting that scanned-receipt PDFs should be rasterized via pdf2image and then routed through the same per-image pipeline (not treated as native PDF text).

confidence.rationale: Field-level feedback precisely localizes four failing cells (078 amount, 074 amount, 077 amount, 034 date). Visual inspection of those receipts plus the trajectory of in-flight fixes (broadening exclusions, moving to candidate-list voting, two-line fallback misfires) makes the root causes unambiguous for F1, F2, F3, F5, F6. F4's exact failure mode (OCR 03→08 vs locale ambiguity) cannot be fully disambiguated without the OCR text per variant, so the recommendation covers both.
confidence.caveats: Recommendations are stated as skill-document changes only (image-ocr, xlsx, openai-vision, pdf, video-frame-extraction). No oracle answer values were read or inferred; all failure examples come from field_feedback booleans and visible receipt content.

observed_failures.evidence: Receipt (Perniagaan Zheng Hui) shows a single clearly printed date 'Date: 09/03/2018' in DD/MM/YYYY form. Predicted ISO date transposes to month=08, day=09, which cannot be produced by any pattern in DATE_PATTERNS from that string. Indicates OCR mis-read of the slash-separated date or a second date-like token elsewhere on the receipt was matched first.

observed_failures.failure_mode: wrong number picked for Grand Total
observed_failures.evidence: Receipt (Thai Delicious Restaurant) clearly shows 'Total : 92.80' and 'Grand Total : 92.80' with 'Cash Received : 100.00' and 'Change : 7.20' and 'AVERAGE / PAX(S) : 23.20'. '702.00' does not appear anywhere on the printed receipt. This is consistent with (a) OCR mis-reading '92.80' as something like '702' or (b) selecting a non-total line (e.g., concatenating qty/price columns like '7 2.50 2.50' into '702.00') because the extractor only trusted one OCR pass instead of voting across variants, and did not restrict the total-number regex to a `d+\.dd` form on the matched line.

observed_failures.failure_mode: picked pre-rounding Total rather than final TOTAL line
observed_failures.evidence: Receipt (Banh Mi CafE) shows 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26', 'Rounding Adj: -0.01', then 'TOTAL: 23.25'. The task's priority list puts bare 'TOTAL' in the lowest tier, so the extractor matched the earlier 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' line in a higher tier and short-circuited. The final 'TOTAL: 23.25' line is the intended grand total after rounding adjustment.

observed_failures.failure_mode: empty string written instead of null for failed extraction
observed_failures.evidence: Receipt (Daiso/AEON) prints 'Sub-total 5.90', 'Total Sales Incl GST 5.90', 'Total After Adj Incl GST 5.90', 'CASH 10.00'. A correct extractor should return '5.90'. Instead the delivered Excel cell contains the empty string '' (not a real null). Two defects: (1) the extractor failed on a readable 'Total Sales Incl GST' / 'Total After Adj Incl GST' line because neither keyword is in the priority list; (2) when extraction fails, the pipeline writes '' instead of None, violating the task's 'value is set to null' contract.

root_causes.summary: Priority-tier total extraction picks the first keyword match and does not re-evaluate later, more authoritative 'TOTAL' lines that appear after rounding/adjustment rows.
root_causes.detail: When a receipt has 'Total (Inclusive of GST): X' followed by 'Rounding Adj' and then a final standalone 'TOTAL: Y', the current tier design treats the earlier 'Total ...' as a Tier-3/4 match and short-circuits. Final 'TOTAL' after rounding is the canonical grand total but is only considered at the same tier.

root_causes.summary: Keyword list for totals does not cover common Malaysian POS variants.
root_causes.detail: Variants like 'Total Sales Incl GST', 'Total After Adj Incl GST', 'Total RM Incl. of GST', 'Rounded Total', 'Total Inclusive of GST', 'Takeout Total', 'Total Rounded', 'Net Total' are not all reliably matched by the current priority tiers, causing total extraction to fall through to None (or to garbage via fallback).

root_causes.summary: Total/date extraction trusts a single OCR pass per image and has no variant-level agreement/voting, so a single mis-read on a small, fragile numeric line propagates directly to output.
root_causes.detail: The original image-ocr skill documents multi-pass OCR but does not require the receipt extractor to vote across preprocessing/PSM variants and take the majority candidate. Impossible outputs like '702.00' for a '92.80' receipt would be rejected by majority agreement across variants.

root_causes.summary: On extraction failure the pipeline wrote '' into the Excel cell, but the task contract requires a real null (empty cell).
root_causes.detail: The downstream xlsx writer did not coerce missing extractions to None and did not force the column dtype to object. Any str('') or NaN that leaks through becomes a non-null cell that the line-by-line grader compares as a mismatch.

root_causes.summary: Date extraction takes the first regex hit in reading order without sanity-checking against other dates on the receipt or against the DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY disambiguation.
root_causes.detail: A single mis-OCRed digit can turn '09/03/2018' into a string that still parses as a valid DD/MM/YYYY date but with swapped fields, or a secondary date-like token (GST id, invoice number with slashes, time-stamped 'Print Date' etc.) is matched instead of the primary 'Date:' line.

root_causes.summary: Extracted totals are not validated against a plausible receipt-amount shape (≤~6 digits before the decimal, exactly two decimals, within a sane magnitude for the item list).
root_causes.detail: A result like '702.00' from a receipt whose items sum to under 100 should be flagged and demoted in favor of an alternate candidate. The current code accepts any regex-matching number on the keyword line.

defects: Priority tiers for receipt totals do not include 'TOTAL SALES INCL GST', 'TOTAL AFTER ADJ INCL GST', 'TOTAL RM INCL(. OF) GST', 'ROUNDED TOTAL', 'TOTAL INCLUSIVE OF GST', 'TOTAL ROUNDED', 'TAKEOUT TOTAL'.

Tier evaluation short-circuits on the first match in reading order; it does not prefer the last qualifying match when several totals of the same tier appear (needed to pick the post-rounding 'TOTAL' line).
No rule to prefer a later 'TOTAL' line over an earlier 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' when a 'Rounding Adj' line appears between them.
No requirement that the chosen number be a strict d+\.dd (or d{1,3}(,d{3})*\.dd) token, with currency prefixes/suffixes stripped — permits ingesting concatenated digits from adjacent columns.
Multi-pass OCR is described but the receipt-field extractor is not required to run multiple preprocess/PSM variants and vote on the total/date candidates.
Date extraction returns the first regex hit instead of preferring the token on a line containing 'DATE', 'INVOICE DATE', or 'PRINT DATE', then falling back to earliest valid match.
No per-image try/except guarantee: a crash on one image can skip a row rather than emitting a row with (None, None).
Strict-schema section does not state explicitly that failed extractions must be written as Python None (not '' and not 'NaN'), and does not show a defensive coercion step before to_excel.

Does not require re-reading the produced file and asserting that (a) empty extractions appear as real nulls, (b) total_amount values match ^\d+\.\d{2}$, (c) date values match ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$ or are null, before finishing.
Does not warn that pandas will silently coerce a mixed None/str column to object only if dtype is forced; otherwise NaN leaks in and is rendered as a non-null string by some readers.

No guidance for using vision OCR as a tie-breaker for Tesseract on receipts where the chosen total has low cross-variant agreement or fails sanity checks. The skill could be lightly extended to describe a 'confirm-the-total' prompt that returns a single JSON {date, total_amount} and is used only when Tesseract candidates disagree.
No defects relevant to this task; not used.
No defects relevant to this task; not used.

changes: Expand the keyword priority tiers to explicitly cover (case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant): Tier A 'GRAND TOTAL'; Tier B 'TOTAL\s*:?\s*RM', 'TOTAL RM'; Tier C 'TOTAL AMOUNT'; Tier D 'ROUNDED TOTAL', 'TOTAL ROUNDED', 'TOTAL AFTER ADJ INCL GST', 'TOTAL SALES INCL GST', 'TOTAL RM INCL(. OF) GST', 'TOTAL INCLUSIVE OF GST', 'NETT? TOTAL', 'NET TOTAL', 'TAKEOUT TOTAL', 'TOTAL DUE', 'AMOUNT DUE', 'BALANCE DUE', '\bTOTAL\b', '\bAMOUNT\b'. Keep the existing exclusion keywords.

Change tier evaluation so that within the matched tier the extractor picks the LAST non-excluded occurrence in reading order (not the first). Rationale: receipts typically print intermediate totals first and the final grand total last, especially after 'Rounding Adj'.
Add a rule: if a 'ROUNDING ADJ' / 'ROUNDING ADJUSTMENT' line is detected, only totals that appear after that line are eligible for selection; if none, fall back to the earlier candidate.

Tighten the number regex used on the chosen line to r'(?<![A-Z0-9])(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*|\d+)\.(\d{2})(?![A-Z0-9])' and reject any candidate that does not have exactly two decimals; strip 'RM'/'MYR'/'$' prefixes, strip commas, then format with f"{v:.2f}".

Require multi-pass OCR for receipt total/date extraction: run at least {grayscale+autocontrast, inverted, sharpened, 2x upscaled} × {--psm 6, --psm 4, --psm 11}, extract a (total, date) candidate from each, and output the majority-voted candidate; break ties by preferring the candidate from --psm 6 on the autocontrast variant.
Add a sanity check: discard total candidates whose magnitude is >10x the median of all other candidates found on the same image (catches '702.00' vs '92.80').

Date extraction: scan line-by-line, prefer the match on a line whose uppercased text contains 'DATE' (but not 'PRINT DATE' if a non-print 'Date' line also exists, and not 'EXP' / 'EXPIRY'); only fall back to the first valid date anywhere. Keep DD/MM/YYYY as the first pattern tried, and when both DD/MM/YYYY and MM/DD/YYYY parses are valid, prefer DD/MM/YYYY (Malaysian receipt convention consistent with this corpus).

Explicitly document the per-image contract: process_receipt(path) must return {'date': str|None, 'total_amount': str|None}, must never raise, and on any internal exception must return {'date': None, 'total_amount': None} so the batch still produces a row.
Document that the returned total_amount is a string formatted f"{v:.2f}" and must never be a float, '', 'None', or 'NaN'.

In the Strict-Schema section, add a bullet that failed extractions must be written as Python None (which becomes a real empty cell), and show the three-step pattern: build list of dicts with None for failures → DataFrame → df[col] = df[col].astype('object') for every string-typed column, then to_excel(..., index=False, sheet_name=exact_name).

Add a re-read verification snippet that asserts, for the output of this family of tasks: the single sheet name matches exactly; columns match exactly; rows are sorted lexicographically by filename; every non-null total_amount matches ^\d+\.\d{2}$; every non-null date matches ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$; empty extractions are real nulls (pd.isna is True) and are not the strings '', 'None', 'NaN', 'nan'.
Call out that pandas will silently coerce a numeric-looking string column to float unless dtype 'object' is enforced, which would turn '47.70' into 47.7 and break grading.

Add a short 'receipt field confirmation' recipe: given an image and a list of Tesseract candidate (total, date) tuples, call gpt-4o with detail=high and the prompt 'Return ONLY JSON {"date":"YYYY-MM-DD or null","total_amount":"N.NN or null"} for the grand total actually paid on this receipt'. Describe it as a tie-breaker only (invoked when majority voting across Tesseract variants is inconclusive or the top candidate fails the sanity check), not as the default path.
No changes required.
No changes required.

confidence.notes: High confidence that RC1 (prefer last TOTAL after rounding), RC2 (missing keyword variants), and RC4 (null vs empty string) are exact root causes for 077 and 078, respectively, because the receipt text is unambiguously visible and matches the predictions' failure shape. Medium-high confidence on RC3 for 074 (702.00 is clearly impossible on a 92.80 Thai-restaurant receipt and is best explained by a single-pass OCR mis-read of the Grand Total line or confusion with the quantity column; majority voting across variants would catch it). Medium confidence on RC5 for 034 because the exact OCR string is not in evidence, but the predicted 2018-08-09 cannot come from a correct read of '09/03/2018' under the documented patterns, so either the primary date line was mis-OCRed or a secondary date-like token was picked. The recommended fixes generalize to any receipt corpus and do not depend on oracle values for these 22 images.

observed_failures.pattern: When a receipt prints an intermediate 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' line followed by a final 'TOTAL:' line after rounding adjustment, the extractor returned the intermediate value because the generic TOTAL/AMOUNT tier scans top-to-bottom and short-circuits on the first match.
observed_failures.evidence: Receipt text order: 'Total (Excluding GST): 21.30' → 'Serv. Charge (3%): 0.65' → 'GST payable (6%): 1.31' → 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' → 'Rounding Adj: -0.01' → 'TOTAL: 23.25'.

observed_failures.pattern: Extraction failure wrote an empty string into the Excel cell instead of a real null. Delivered predictions row for 078 shows total_amount="", not null.
observed_failures.evidence: Predictions row {"filename":"078.jpg", ..., "total_amount":""}; strict-schema xlsx contract requires Python None / pd.NA for missing values.

observed_failures.pattern: Single-pass tesseract misread a leading '1' as '7' on the final total line ('Total Incl. of GST 102.00'). No cross-pass sanity check to prefer the plausible value.
observed_failures.evidence: Receipt body shows Subtotal 102.00, Total Incl. of GST 102.00, Payment 102.00; repeated 102.00 values would have outvoted a single 702.00 misread.

observed_failures.pattern: Month digit '3' misread as '8' on a dd/mm/yyyy date. No cross-pass voting or sanity filter on dates either.
observed_failures.evidence: Receipt date line reads 'Date: 09/03/2018' with the same '3' glyph repeating elsewhere; a multi-pass vote would have resolved it.

root_causes.cause: Within a priority tier, the loop iterates lines top-to-bottom and returns the first keyword match. Receipts routinely print the final, post-rounding TOTAL at the bottom; intermediate 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' lines are matched first by the generic \bTOTAL\b keyword and win.
root_causes.fix_direction: For the lowest-specificity tier (bare TOTAL/AMOUNT/BALANCE DUE/etc.), scan bottom-up so the final printed total is preferred. Higher-specificity tiers (GRAND TOTAL, TOTAL RM, NETT TOTAL) can stay top-down since they are already unambiguous.

root_causes.cause: The documented pipeline permits returning Python None, but downstream code paths can convert that to '' (e.g., via str(None), dict.get(k,''), or coercion through a string column before to_excel). The candidate xlsx skill warns against '' but does not show a defensive final-step null coercion before writing.
root_causes.fix_direction: Make null handling a single enforced step: after assembling the DataFrame, replace any '', 'None', 'NaN', 'nan' in the date/total_amount columns with None, and assert dtype==object before to_excel.

root_causes.where: image-ocr → multi_pass_ocr() is defined but not used for value selection
root_causes.cause: multi_pass_ocr() concatenates all variants' text, so a single bad variant can inject a wrong candidate (e.g., '702.00') that the keyword/priority logic then picks. There is no per-variant extraction + majority vote on the final tuple.
root_causes.fix_direction: Run (preprocessing × PSM) variants, call extract_date / extract_total on EACH variant independently, then majority-vote the non-null (date, amount) values. Prefer values that appear in ≥2 variants; break ties toward the higher-specificity tier.

root_causes.cause: Only the first regex hit is returned. When OCR produces a plausible but wrong date (single-glyph confusion), there is no secondary check against other date-like strings on the same receipt (e.g., PRINT date, timestamp, invoice number containing the year).
root_causes.fix_direction: Collect all date candidates, cross-pass vote, and prefer dates whose year and month also appear in a nearby timestamp or invoice-number substring on the same receipt.

skill_defects.defect: Top-down first-match returns intermediate pre-rounding totals on receipts where the final TOTAL appears after a rounding-adjustment line.
skill_defects.generalization: Applies to any receipt format with 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' + 'Rounding Adj' + final 'TOTAL'.

skill_defects.defect: Concatenates variant outputs instead of extracting per variant and voting, so noisy variants contaminate the keyword search.
skill_defects.generalization: Applies to any receipt where tesseract is sensitive to preprocessing (faded prints, dark backgrounds, low DPI).

skill_defects.defect: Returns the first regex match without cross-pass voting or intra-receipt corroboration (timestamp/invoice fields).
skill_defects.generalization: Applies to any receipt with single-glyph digit confusion (3↔8, 1↔7, 0↔8, 5↔6).

skill_defects.defect: Pattern trusts caller to supply None; lacks a mandatory final normalization step that coerces '', 'None', 'NaN' → None on date and total_amount columns before to_excel.
skill_defects.generalization: Any pipeline where extractors can leak empty strings will silently fail the grader on missing-value receipts.

skill_defects.defect: Missing an explicit verify step that non-null total_amount strings match the regex ^\d+\.\d{2}$ and that date strings match ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$; checklist currently only spot-checks decimals.
skill_defects.generalization: Avoids silent coercions (e.g., floats that render as '23.2' instead of '23.20').

repair_recommendations.change: In extract_total, for the lowest-specificity tier (bare TOTAL / AMOUNT / TOTAL DUE / AMOUNT DUE / BALANCE DUE / NETT TOTAL), iterate matching lines in reverse (bottom-up) and return the first hit. Keep higher-specificity tiers (GRAND TOTAL, TOTAL RM, TOTAL AMOUNT) top-down.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Receipts print the final, after-rounding total last; higher-specificity labels are unique so direction does not matter.

repair_recommendations.change: Add a dedicated exclusion pattern for 'TOTAL (INCLUSIVE OF GST)', 'TOTAL INCLUSIVE GST', 'TOTAL INCL. OF GST', and 'TOTAL INCL GST' ONLY when a later line in the same receipt also matches a TOTAL keyword after a 'ROUNDING' line. If no later TOTAL exists, keep the inclusive-GST line as the fallback.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Preserves correct behavior on receipts without a post-rounding final total (many single-item receipts) while fixing the 077-style pattern.

repair_recommendations.change: Refactor multi_pass_ocr into multi_pass_extract(image_path) that: (a) runs N preprocessing × PSM variants, (b) calls extract_date and extract_total on each variant's text, (c) returns the majority-voted (date, total_amount) pair, breaking ties toward values that came from a higher-specificity keyword tier and toward values present on the receipt image more than once.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Mitigates single-glyph digit confusion for both date and amount (034, 074) without changing deterministic batch ordering.

repair_recommendations.change: In extract_date, collect ALL regex candidates across formats, then prefer the candidate whose YYYY also appears in a nearby timestamp line (e.g., '… HH:MM' or 'DATE/TIME') and whose MM matches at least one other digit substring near the same line. Fallback to the first candidate if no corroboration.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Intra-receipt corroboration reduces date-digit misreads where the timestamp confirms the correct month/year.

repair_recommendations.change: Explicitly document and implement: on ANY exception or extraction failure, return Python None (not '', not 'None', not 0.0). Add a small post-extraction validator: if total_amount is not None, assert re.fullmatch(r'\d+\.\d{2}', value); if date is not None, assert re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', value); otherwise set to None.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Guarantees nulls are real nulls and non-nulls are grader-shaped.

repair_recommendations.change: Add a mandatory final normalization block to the Canonical Pattern: df[['date','total_amount']] = df[['date','total_amount']].astype('object'); then df.replace({'': None, 'None': None, 'NaN': None, 'nan': None}, inplace=True); then re-assert types.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Enforces the real-null contract at the writer layer even when upstream extractors leak sentinel strings.

repair_recommendations.change: Extend the Contract Checklist with two regex asserts: for every non-null row, re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', date) and re.fullmatch(r'\d+\.\d{2}', total_amount); re-open the written file with pd.read_excel and re-check.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Catches float→'23.2' and other string-coercion drifts before the grader does.

repair_recommendations.change: Document that the extraction output must be a list of plain dicts with pre-stringified fields, and that pandas should NOT be given a Series of mixed float/str for total_amount — enforce astype('object') on construction.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Prevents accidental re-coercion to float when a single row's string happens to be numeric-parseable.

confidence.notes: F1/F2 fixes directly address the observed 077 and 078 failures via skill-logic changes. F3/F4 are OCR-noise driven; multi-pass per-variant voting is a sound mitigation but cannot guarantee resolution on every digit misread. All recommendations are confined to the five existing SKILL.md files and generalize to any receipt batch with the same priority/exclusion/null contract.

observed_failures.evidence: Prediction row for 078.jpg has total_amount = "" (empty string). The task contract and the current xlsx skill require real nulls (None) for unextractable fields; an empty string is a schema/format violation distinct from a genuine OCR miss.
observed_failures.impact: Guaranteed amount mismatch for any receipt where extraction fails; converts a soft miss into a hard format error.

observed_failures.evidence: Receipt shows a sequence: 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26', then 'Rounding Adj: -0.01', then 'TOTAL: 23.25'. Prediction picked 23.26 (first TOTAL-tier hit) instead of the final rounded TOTAL on the standalone 'TOTAL:' line.
observed_failures.impact: Any receipt with an intermediate '(Inclusive of GST)/(Incl. GST)'/pre-rounding total followed by a later final TOTAL will be mis-extracted.

observed_failures.evidence: Prediction 702.00. The receipt's 'Subtotal: 102.00 / Total Incl. of GST: 102.00 / Total Amt Rounded: 102.00' lines were recognized but the leading digit '1' was OCR'd as '7'. No cross-check across the multiple repeated totals or multiple OCR variants was used to resolve the digit.

root_causes.description: The xlsx skill's 'strict schema' guidance names the rule ('write real nulls, never ""/"None"/NaN') only as a checklist bullet and in prose. The canonical code pattern shows `None` in the rows list but does not include a post-construction normalization step that coerces any falsy/empty/sentinel value to None, nor a post-write verification that scans the written cells for '' or 'nan'. Agents can easily default to `'' ` in except-branches or when a sub-extractor returns an empty string.

The current image-ocr skill's `extract_total` iterates tiers in priority order but, within a tier, picks the FIRST matching line. Real receipts place the authoritative TOTAL at the bottom and often precede it with qualified variants ('Total (Inclusive of GST)', 'Total RM Incl. of GST', 'Takeout Total (incl GST)', 'Total Excl. of GST', 'Nett Total vs Total'). No rule prefers (a) the latest match within a tier, (b) standalone unqualified 'TOTAL' over parenthetically-qualified ones, or (c) rounded/final totals over pre-rounding totals. The exclusion list also omits 'INCLUSIVE OF GST', 'INCL GST', 'INCL. OF GST', 'EXCL. OF GST', 'EXCLUDING GST', 'EXCLUSIVE GST', 'ROUNDED TOTAL' vs 'TOTAL ROUNDED', 'TAKEOUT TOTAL', 'SERVICE CHARGE'.

`multi_pass_ocr` concatenates text from all variants but downstream extractors (`extract_total`, `extract_date`) run once on the concatenated blob and return the first plausible hit. There is no voting across variants, no agreement check across multiple candidate lines (e.g., Subtotal / Total / Rounded Total all showing the same number), and no rejection of implausible OCR artifacts (leading-7 vs leading-1 for an amount that also appears elsewhere as a leading-1).

Priority regex patterns demand clean whitespace and exact spellings ('GRAND\s*TOTAL', 'TOTAL\s*:?\s*RM'). OCR commonly corrupts separators: 'GrandTota.', 'Grand Tota)', 'T0TAL', 'TOTAL RH', 'TOTAL AMT', 'NET AMOUNT', 'AMOUNT PAYABLE'. There is no normalization step (uppercase + strip punctuation + collapse whitespace + common OCR digit/letter swaps like 0↔O, 1↔I↔l, 5↔S) before matching, and no fuzzy/edit-distance fallback for the 'GRAND TOTAL' tier.

`_last_number` accepts any token matching the number regex on the keyword line, including stray digits from line numbers, dates, phone numbers, or item codes that OCR may have run into the TOTAL line. There is no check that the numeric is monetary-shaped (e.g., has exactly two decimal places or starts with a currency affix), no preference for a two-decimal candidate, and no cross-check that the chosen value agrees with other totals on the receipt.

`extract_date` walks a fixed pattern list and returns on the first match. There is no disambiguation using additional date-like fields on the receipt (print date, invoice date, transaction date) and no rejection of implausible dates (future, pre-2000, impossible day/month). Running the date extractor on multiple OCR variants and voting would correct many single-digit misreads.

The image-ocr skill provides building blocks (`process_receipt`, `multi_pass_ocr`, `extract_total`, `extract_date`) but no top-level 'canonical batch pipeline' that the agent can call once and write. This invites iterative per-image debugging, which both wastes iterations and introduces regressions such as writing '' instead of None.

defects: `extract_total` picks the first matching line within a tier; should prefer the LAST match and prefer standalone 'TOTAL' over parenthetically-qualified totals.

OF GST', 'EXCLUSIVE OF GST', 'SERVICE CHARGE', 'SERV CHARGE', 'ROUNDING', 'ROUNDING ADJ', 'ROUNDING ADJUSTMENT', 'TAKEOUT TOTAL', 'TAX AMT', 'TAX AMOUNT', 'TAX TOTAL', 'TOTAL EXCL', 'TOTAL BEFORE', 'CASH', 'VISA', 'MASTERCARD', 'PAYMENT', 'CARD', 'MYR', 'POINTS', 'SAVING', 'DISCOUNT'.
Keyword regex is not applied to a normalized line (no uppercase+punctuation-strip+whitespace-collapse+OCR-swap preprocessing), so OCR-corrupted labels like 'GrandTota.' silently fail the top tier.
No cross-variant voting: `multi_pass_ocr` concatenates variant outputs, but `extract_total`/`extract_date` ignore which variant each candidate came from and do not break ties by agreement count.

Date pipeline returns on first match and does not run across multiple OCR variants with majority voting, so a single misread digit flips the date.

`process_receipt` has no post-condition guarding that results are either a valid formatted string or `None` — any downstream caller that stores the extractor's raw return into an Excel cell can leak '' or stray text.
No top-level batch function that composes sorted-directory iteration + `process_receipt` + a DataFrame row dict, so each agent reinvents (and sometimes breaks) the glue code.

Strict-schema section lists 'write None, not ""/NaN' only as prose and a checklist item; the canonical code pattern does not include an explicit normalization pass (e.g., `df = df.where(df.notna() & (df != ''), None)`) nor a self-verification loop that reads the file back and asserts no cell contains '', 'None', 'NaN', or 'nan'.

No explicit pattern for 'if an upstream extractor can return either a formatted string or None, wrap it with: value = value if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip() else None' before DataFrame construction.
Verification snippet checks that non-null totals match 'N.NN' but does not assert that any cell written as a null is actually read back as NaN/None (catching the '' bug).

root_causes.description: Null-value contract not enforced at the writer boundary: empty strings leak through for failed extractions, violating the 'null on failure' requirement.

Within-tier tiebreak for TOTAL keyword picks the FIRST matching line encountered. When multiple lines in the same tier qualify (e.g., 'Total (Inclusive of GST):' and 'TOTAL:'), the unqualified/final TOTAL line (typically the bottom-most, post-rounding value) is overridden by an earlier, pre-adjustment line.

Multi-pass OCR output is concatenated into a single blob before keyword/number extraction. This lets a lower-quality pass inject wrong digits into the SAME keyword line as a higher-quality pass, and the first-match rule then selects the corrupted number.

Date extraction scans all date-shaped tokens in reading order without anchoring to a 'Date'/'DATE' label, so OCR digit confusion in nearby non-date tokens (times, transaction numbers) can produce plausible-looking but wrong dates.

Preprocessing/variant set is small and generic; it lacks a digit-focused rescue pass (character whitelist, additional PSM-7 single-line crop around total keyword) that reliably recovers money amounts on faint/low-contrast receipts.

Preprocessing recipe does not include a digit-focused rescue path (character whitelist, PSM-7 on a cropped band near the total keyword) for faint monetary totals.

root_causes.summary: No explicit locale rule for DD/MM/YYYY-dominant Malaysian receipts; the ad-hoc dateutil-style parsing (or first-match pattern) can flip day/month when both are <=12.
root_causes.scope: image-ocr skill — date extraction guidance is absent in original SKILL.md; candidate adds patterns but still only tries the first matching format and does not document that dmy must take precedence over mdy for this corpus.

root_causes.summary: Total extraction uses first keyword hit within a tier. Receipts commonly show a sequence 'Total (Excl GST) -> Total (Incl GST) -> Rounding Adj -> TOTAL/Grand Total'; picking the first match returns an intermediate value.
root_causes.scope: image-ocr skill — the candidate's extract_total iterates top-to-bottom and returns on the first match; it does not differentiate qualified vs final totals and does not add qualifier-based exclusions (EXCLUDING, INCLUSIVE OF, BEFORE ROUNDING).

root_causes.summary: Single-variant OCR output is accepted as the source of truth for the amount. Common glyph confusions (1↔7, 0↔8, 5↔6, O↔0) corrupt digits like 102.00 -> 702.00. No cross-validation against other occurrences of the same figure on the receipt (subtotal/total/payment/change-back).
root_causes.scope: image-ocr skill — multi_pass_ocr exists but concatenates text; it does not cast votes across variants, nor does it cross-check amount candidates against other numeric fields that typically agree (subtotal == total when GST already inclusive and discount==0).

root_causes.summary: On tabular receipts (Thai Delicious, Perniagaan Zheng Hui) the amount is in a right-aligned column far from the label; OCR preserves them on the same line only with --psm 6/4. If the chosen PSM breaks the line, the keyword line has no number and the two-line fallback also fails because the next line is another label.
root_causes.scope: image-ocr skill — the two-line fallback is too narrow; it should also look forward 1–2 lines for a token that looks like 'last number on the row anchored at the keyword's y-coordinate', and the skill should recommend image_to_data with block/line numbers to preserve row grouping on tabular layouts.

root_causes.summary: On extraction failure, an empty string was written into the Excel cell instead of a real Python None. The xlsx strict-schema skill mentions this but does not enforce a normalize-before-write step, and does not show a post-write re-read check that would catch '' or 'nan' cells.
root_causes.scope: xlsx skill — the Canonical Pattern is correct in spirit but relies on the caller returning None; it should mandate an explicit sanitize step (replace '', 'None', 'nan', NaN -> None) immediately before to_excel, and extend the self-check to assert no cell is the string ''.

root_causes.summary: The source run hit max_iterations=65 and terminated without a finish; there is no evidence of a final re-read assertion loop on the produced Excel (dtype of total_amount strings, ordering, sheet name, null presence).
root_causes.scope: xlsx skill (and image-ocr batch orchestration) — the skills do not require a terminal self-check that re-opens the output and asserts the strict-schema contract before claiming done.

skill_defects.defect: Date extraction section is absent in the original and under-specified in the candidate: no explicit DD/MM/YYYY precedence rule, no handling of 2-digit years, no guidance to skip plausibly-wrong dates (e.g., future dates, printer-footer timestamps that duplicate the invoice date in a different format).

extract_total picks the first keyword hit within each priority tier. It does not prefer the LAST matching candidate within a tier, and it does not treat qualifier parentheticals ('Excluding GST', 'Inclusive of GST', 'Before Rounding', 'Rounded') as either exclusions or de-prioritizers.

Exclusion list is incomplete for this receipt family. Missing: 'ROUNDING', 'ROUNDED' (when used as a line label alone), 'SERVICE CHARGE' / 'SVC CHG', 'CASH', 'VISA', 'MASTERCARD', 'PAYMENT', 'CASH RECEIVED', 'POINTS', 'TAX AMT', 'EXC GST'. Several of these produced ambiguity in 063/064/087/088/097 and were only saved by other heuristics.

Multi-pass OCR output is a concatenated string, not a vote. There is no recommended consensus/majority mechanism across preprocessing variants and PSM modes, so a single bad pass can corrupt the final amount even when other passes read it correctly.

No cross-field numeric sanity check. On most receipts, extracted total should equal one of: subtotal, cash tendered - change, sum of line items, or the amount printed next to CASH/VISA/MASTERCARD. The skill never leverages this redundancy to reject obvious OCR errors like 702.00 vs. four co-occurring 102.00 values.

Tabular-layout extraction is unaddressed. For receipts where label and amount are on the same visual row but separated by whitespace columns, the skill should recommend using pytesseract.image_to_data and grouping tokens by (block_num, par_num, line_num) so the amount on the same row as 'GRAND TOTAL' is recoverable even when --psm 6 splits it.

Strict-Schema section does not enforce a pre-write normalization step that coerces '', 'None', 'nan', NaN, and numeric-looking floats for string-typed columns into the correct representation. The example writes the dict directly; it should wrap each field in a small normalize() helper.

The Pitfalls checklist does not include an assertion recipe that opens the written file with openpyxl (not pandas) and checks that nullable cells are value=None (not ''), that string columns have cell.data_type == 's', and that the sheet set is exactly the one required.

There is no shared 'stop condition' recipe: an end-of-pipeline self-check that re-reads the produced artifact and confirms the task contract, independent of the iteration budget. This leaves the run vulnerable to silent failure when max_iterations is reached mid-polish.

repair_recommendations.change: State explicitly that for receipt-style corpora the DD/MM/YYYY and DD/MM/YY formats take precedence over MM/DD. Try (%d/%m/%Y, %d-%m-%Y, %d/%m/%y, %d-%m-%y, %d %b %Y, %d-%b-%Y, %Y-%m-%d, %Y/%m/%d) IN THAT ORDER. Reject dates that parse to the future relative to today or whose month/day is impossible; when two different dates are present, prefer the one on the line containing the token 'DATE' and co-located with a time stamp.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Fixes 034.jpg's day/month flip and generalizes to any receipt where both components are ≤12.

repair_recommendations.change: Replace the concatenation example with a 'consensus voter': run N preprocessing × PSM variants, apply extract_total and extract_date to each variant independently, and return the modal (most frequent) non-null result; break ties by preferring variants whose average per-word confidence from image_to_data is highest.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Mitigates single-digit OCR corruption like 102.00 → 702.00 on 074.jpg; generalizes to all glyph-confusion failures.

repair_recommendations.section: NEW subsection: Cross-Field Numeric Sanity Check
repair_recommendations.change: Add guidance that after extracting a candidate total, scan the OCR text for other amounts that appear on lines containing SUBTOTAL, CASH, PAYMENT, TOTAL ROUNDED, or 'Cash Received - Change'. If the candidate disagrees with ≥2 of these redundant values that mutually agree, replace the candidate with the modal redundant value. Include a short worked example (safety-pins receipt: payment/subtotal/rounded all agree at 102.00; candidate 702.00 is overridden).
repair_recommendations.rationale: Directly repairs 074.jpg and gives generic robustness against single-digit OCR errors on well-structured receipts.

repair_recommendations.section: NEW subsection: Tabular-Layout Recovery via image_to_data
repair_recommendations.change: Recommend grouping pytesseract.image_to_data tokens by (block_num, par_num, line_num) and extracting the right-most numeric token on any line whose leftmost tokens match a priority keyword. Provide a small snippet. State that this is the preferred fallback whenever the string-based line scanner returns None on a keyword-rich receipt.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Addresses 078.jpg (and future tabular layouts) where the label and amount are same-row but visually far apart; prevents silent empty extractions.

repair_recommendations.section: Structured Field Extraction — Per-Image Pipeline with Null-Safe Failure
repair_recommendations.change: Explicitly state the extractor MUST return Python None (never '', 'None', 'nan', 0, or 0.0) on failure, and MUST NOT swallow partial successes (e.g., returning '23.' because the decimal portion was cut). Add a validation regex `^\d+\.\d{2}$` applied to every returned total string, with None as the fallback on mismatch.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Prevents the 078.jpg empty-string writer drift and any similar partial-amount leakage.

repair_recommendations.change: Insert a mandatory normalize_row() step before DataFrame construction that maps any of {'', 'None', 'none', 'nan', 'NaN', float('nan'), pd.NA} to None for every cell, and that re-formats numeric-looking totals through f'{float(x):.2f}' only when the value already matches the two-decimal regex. Show the normalize step in the code example, not as an afterthought.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Guarantees nulls are real nulls (fixes 078.jpg write-side bug) and prevents accidental float coercion of already-correct strings.

repair_recommendations.change: Expand the self-check to open the file with openpyxl (not pandas) and assert: wb.sheetnames == ['results']; header row equals the expected tuple; for each non-null cell in string-typed columns cell.data_type == 's'; no cell equals '' or 'nan'; row count equals input count; filenames are lexicographically sorted. Fail loudly if any assertion trips so the agent re-attempts before its iteration budget expires.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Catches writer-side strict-schema drift (empty strings, wrong dtype, wrong sheet name) that currently flips binary reward to 0 despite high field accuracy.

repair_recommendations.section: NEW subsection: Terminal Self-Check (required before claiming done)
repair_recommendations.change: Add a short checklist and code snippet to be run as the final step of any pipeline that produces a graded Excel: re-open, verify schema, verify ordering, verify null representation, verify string-amount two-decimal regex on all non-null totals; only then emit the finish signal. Note that this check must run even when the agent is near its iteration budget.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Mitigates RC6 (max_iterations termination without self-verification); the same pattern applies to any strict-schema task, not just OCR.

repair_recommendations.change: Add checks: 'Chosen total line is the LAST matching line within its tier'; 'Candidate total agrees with ≥1 redundant field (subtotal/payment/rounded/cash-change) when such fields are present'; 'Date is DD/MM-first and not in the future'; 'All failures surface as Python None, never empty string'.
repair_recommendations.rationale: Formalizes the new invariants so they are testable during the agent's own review loop.
